#2227. Galli reveals details of Cardinale’s speech at legends dinner: “Heartfelt and sincere”

Before the Inter game, AC Milan invited several legends to a dinner hosted by Gerry Cardinale to honour them.

In recent years, there has maybe been an avoidance of celebrating the club’s history. Iconic players have been overlooked and the past hasn’t been at the forefront. Of course, the present takes precedence, but it’s almost like the rich history of Milan has been overlooked.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been a few nods to the past, as well as a few kits with historic hints. Yet, you’d be lying if you said that the club were completely honouring the legends that had represented them before.

Now, things are seemingly changing. The Hall of Fame presentation was the most public display of affection, but Cardinale also hosted a dinner for the club’s legends. In attendance of the dinner was Filippo Galli, and he’s offered some information on what happened, praising the American for the event, as MilanNews relays from his interview with Gazzetta dello Sport.

“He spoke for a good half hour, and I found it to be heartfelt and sincere. I’d particularly emphasise the mea culpa for the mistakes made. I’d say it’s a good start; his words seemed heartfelt, and not necessary. But there’s still a long way to go.

“He insisted that he will continue to invest. I’d say he understands how soccer works in Italy, compared to the American one, where everything is more relaxed.

“He then spoke kindly of Berlusconi’s career at the club, emphasising, however, that Berlusconi would now be dealing with a changed world, where financial sustainability becomes vital. Now we’re waiting for something to happen…

“Right now, there’s a January transfer window to address, a technical area to sort out and define. There’s a need to establish high-level governance; otherwise the coach will be left alone, and if by chance the results don’t arrive…

“Did this dinner organised by Cardinale surprise me? Actually, yes, we weren’t expecting it. The invitation came from Milan a couple of weeks earlier. For us, these are opportunities to meet up with former teammates, to represent Milan. And this, regardless of who owns the club.”

#2224. Watch: De Winter congratulated and Pavlovic absent as Milan train on eve of Ferencvaros game

Ahead of AC Milan’s game against Ferencvaros, a live training session was hosted and a few details have filtered through.

It’s a big game in the Europa League tomorrow; a win would keep Milan in the race for the top eight, anything else will force them to prepare for a Round of 16 knockout tie. It’s a difficult position to be in.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Nevertheless, Ruben Amorim is expected to rotate his squad a little bit, with the average age of his team expected to drop by at least four years, compared to the 28-year-old average of Saturday’s team that won the derby.

Almost everyone trained today, as MilanNews relays, barring a few out with injury – Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze – but they were also joined by the absent Strahinja Pavlovic.

Whilst he’s not injured, his minutes have to be monitored carefully and he could play tomorrow. However, he was given a rest today.

In addition to this, a few players went through ‘the tunnel’ getting slaps, with Koni De Winter celebrated for becoming a father. Additionally, Sankoun Diawara, Diego Moreiera, Adrien Rabiot and coach Carlos Fernandes went through for their work in the derby.

#2223. Pallone d'Oro, Zidane difende Mbappé: "Lo meritava quanto Kane, normale sia deluso"

Il secondo posto al Pallone d'Oro 2026 rappresenta il miglior piazzamento della carriera di Kylian Mbappé, ma lascia inevitabilmente un pizzico di amarezza all'attaccante francese. A conquistare il prestigioso riconoscimento è stato Harry Kane, davanti al capitano della Francia, che sperava di aggiudicarsi il premio dopo una stagione da protagonista. A commentare il risultato è stato Zinédine Zidane, intervenuto ai microfoni di Téléfoot. L'ex fuoriclasse del Real Madrid ha riconosciuto i meriti del connazionale, sottolineando come anche Mbappé avrebbe avuto tutte le carte in regola per conquistare il trofeo.

Interrogato sul secondo posto dell'attaccante, Zidane ha dichiarato: "Il Pallone d'Oro? Ognuno ha le sue preferenze, lui è secondo, dobbiamo solo accettarlo. Ovviamente è deluso perché se lo meritava altrettanto". Parole che testimoniano la stima nei confronti di Mbappé, pur senza mettere in discussione il verdetto che ha premiato Kane. Per il francese resta comunque un risultato importante, il migliore ottenuto finora nella corsa al riconoscimento individuale più prestigioso del calcio mondiale.

Nel corso dell'intervista, Zidane si è soffermato anche sulle condizioni fisiche del capitano francese, costretto ad abbandonare l'ultimo ritiro dopo la prima partita contro la Turchia a causa di un infortunio. "Mbappé? Sarà sicuramente felice di essere tornato in nazionale. La sua prima convocazione è andata come è andata. Sicuramente voleva restare con noi, ma è un giocatore che gioca molto, quindi dobbiamo essere prudenti". Un richiamo alla necessità di gestire con attenzione il carico di impegni dell'attaccante, chiamato a confermarsi protagonista tanto con il club quanto con la nazionale.

#2222. FacileRent Molinari Napoli, presentata la stagione 2026/27: sport, territorio e nuove ambizioni

– Passione, ambizione e vicinanza al territorio. All’insegna di questi aspetti la Molinari Napoli ha presentato il nuovo anno sportivo ed in particolare la stagione della squadra che competerà in Serie B2 femminile. Un evento – quello tenutosi sabato 7 novembre al PalaVesuvio – che ha coinvolto società, istituzioni, partner, staff tecnico e atlete, per raccontare obiettivi, ambizioni e prospettive di un progetto che vuole continuare a investire nello sport e nel territorio.

«Lavoriamo sul territorio da anni, avvicinando i giovani di Ponticelli allo sport. Da cinque anni sentiamo la vicinanza dell’Amministrazione comunale che ci ha aiutato in qualsiasi circostanza», ha dichiarato il Presidente della Molinari Napoli, Gennaro Nappo. «Per la Serie B2 c’è tanta ambizione, voglia di crescere e di essere d’esempio per il settore giovanile. Abbiamo costruito una squadra competitiva e speriamo che il campo ce lo dimostri».

Presenti alla conferenza l’On. Borrelli e l’Ass. Ferrante

«Io non credo più all’idea del centro e delle periferie per come si sta evolvendo il sistema sociale del nostro territorio. Ogni luogo come questo (il PalaVesuvio di Via Argine n.d.r.) è oro colato da valorizzare», ha dichiarato l’Onorevole Francesco Emilio Borrelli, presente alla conferenza stampa. «Lo sport è qualcosa di straordinario non solo perché ci insegna la disciplina, il rispetto del prossimo e l’impegno, ma anche perché ci spinge a fare attività fisica. Noi siamo in questo momento la Regione più obesa d’Italia per quanto riguarda i bambini. Bambini che non fanno sport: è importante fargli fare un’attività pulita e sana». Borrelli ha concluso il suo intervento sottolineando la vicinanza alla squadra: «Verrò sicuramente a vedere una delle vostre partite: tiferò per voi».

«Lo sport è una leva fondamentale, anche se a volte viene considerato secondario, soprattutto per quanto riguarda i supporti economici», ha dichiarato l’Assessora allo Sport ed alle Pari Opportunità del Comune di Napoli, Emanuela Ferrante. «Cinque anni fa, con grande difficoltà, ho provato a recuperare delle somme per riqualificare gli impianti, senza i quali non si può andare da nessuna parte. A conclusione di questo anno, che ha visto Napoli essere Capitale Europea dello Sport, posso dire con fierezza e con grande gioia che abbiamo investito 35 milioni di euro su tanti gli impianti sportivi. Partendo dagli impianti riqualificati si può ambire a realizzare quello che penso sia il diritto di tutti i ragazzi: fare sport».

L’Assessora si è rivolta poi direttamente alla squadra. «Siete una testimonianza ed un esempio per tutte le ragazze ed i ragazzi di Ponticelli. Questa stagione sarà una straordinaria esperienza e cercheremo di far riempire la palestra ogni volta che giocherete in casa».

#2219. Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Joe Westley believes his battle for game time with fellow Dundee attackers will only benefit the Tayside club.

With just one defeat in the last five, the Dark Blues are in fifth place in the William Hill Premiership and the fourth-highest scorers, with Ashley Hay notching three in the last four games and Bradley Fink with four in the last six.

Westley missed three games with an ankle injury but replaced Fink in the 3-1 win over Kilmarnock last Wednesday and, ahead of the Tayside derby against St Johnstone at McDiarmid Park on Saturday, the 22-year-old, with five goals in all competitions this season, said: “I think it’s a healthy competition.

“Everyone wants to be playing football and be in the team. So when we’ve got Ash and Brad scoring, it means I need to up my game and score as many as I can when I’m given the chance because you know that when you’ve got the shirt, people are waiting to take it off you.

“It’s a healthy competition and I think we all drive each other to be the best versions of ourselves.

“I think when all the strikers are scoring and doing well, it’s good to be a part of an attack that’s doing well because you create for each other. If everyone’s firing and everyone’s doing well, then it increases your chance of getting goals and assisting as well.

“It’s a really good time to be an attacker at the club. I think it’s starting to click between everyone and whoever’s on up front has got a great understanding of what’s wanted from them. It gives them the best possible chance to score goals and win games.

“I think everything can come down to hard work. As a group everyone around the club works so hard day in, day out and we’re pushed in training, we’re pushed in the gym and I think we try and always gain the little one percent that we can every week.

“But also there’s the environment that the manager has created where everyone’s in it together. Everyone wants to do the hard yards for each other and I think the hard yards and the basics of football are things that can separate you from other teams in the league.

“I think so far this season we’ve been good at the basics and as long as we continue to do them we’ll be fine.”

#2218. Official: Chukwueze undergoes successful hip surgery in London with Milan doctor present

Entering this season, Samuel Chukwueze was not expected to be a huge player for AC Milan, but he was until his hip injury.

After an alright loan spell with Fulham, most expected Chukwueze to be sold in the summer. The Whites hadn’t taken up their buy option and the Nigerian hadn’t impressed enough to be seen as a guaranteed return.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Nevertheless, Ruben Amorim saw things differently, believing he could play a role. Of course, he’s not the only player who he offered an opportunity to, but he may be the best example of things changing.

The Nigerian was pivotal to Amorim’s system, being the starting wing-back on the right for most of the early season. Unfortunately, though, he suffered a hip injury and hasn’t been seen since.

As confirmed in recent minutes by a club statement, Chukwueze’s surgery has now taken place and it was a complete success. A return date has not been given, but reports from the time of the injury suggested he’d be back in 2027.

“AC Milan announces that Samuel Chukwueze has undergone surgery in London to repair a ruptured tendon in the tensor fascia latae muscle in his left hip. The surgery, performed by Prof. Ernest Schilders in the presence of Dr. Stefano Mazzoni, was a complete success.

“The footballer will return to Italy today, where he will begin his rehabilitation process.”

#2217. Inter, Spence rimugina sul Mondiale: "Non volevamo solo il terzo posto con l'Inghilterra"

"Vengo da Peckham, un quartiere nel Sud di Londra. Qui ho iniziato a giocare, penso che il primo luogo in cui ho preso a calci un pallone non fosse un vero e proprio campo, ma il Peckham Rye Park". Come se fosse ieri per Djed Spence nel rievocare i primi ricordi legati alla sua passione per il calcio e in patria, in Inghilterra, quando ancora fantasticava sui suoi idoli e non giocava ai massimi livelli. "Mi piaceva molto Cristiano Ronaldo quando ero piccolo, provavo a imitarlo quando giocavo al Peckham Town: il mio primo gol è arrivato tanto tempo fa, ma ricordo che l'avevo segnato con una rovesciata. In quel momento ho sentito tantissima energia, correvo per il campo senza fermarmi", ha raccontato ai microfoni ufficiali dell'Inter, dove gioca attualmente.

Invece, sulla sua carriera, non ha mai avuto dubbi. "Ho sempre voluto fare il calciatore, l'ho capito fin dalla prima volta in cui ho messo piede in un campo". E una persona su tutte lo ha aiutato a emergere fortemente nel calcio ad alti livelli: "Steve Cooper: con lui al Nottingham Forest abbiamo conquistato la promozione in Premier League, la prima vera vittoria importante della mia carriera".

Oggi nuovo volto della squadra di Cristian Chivu sulla fascia destra, ha sfoggiato la sua miglior prestazione dall'arrivo in estate contro il Feyenoord. "Il mio giocatore preferito della storia dell'Inter è sicuramente Ronaldo, il Fenomeno. Mi piace molto l'Italia: quando giocavo al Genoa ero rimasto colpito dalle vibrazioni positive di questo Paese, dal clima e dall'ottimo cibo", ha invece sottolineato sui propri gusti personali. Passando, infine, all'amarezza per il terzo posto al Mondiale con la maglia dei Tre Leoni indosso: "Non era il risultato che volevamo, puntavamo alla vittoria. L'Inghilterra però aveva fatto meglio solo nel 1966 quando vinse la Coppa: abbiamo avuto l'opportunità di fare la storia, è stata una bellissima emozione".

#2215. Celtic trigger Turkish TV meltdown as ‘rant of a lifetime’ takes bonkers turn

Celtic’s stunning Europa League comeback sent Turkish TV into meltdown as raging Besiktas pundits struggled to comprehend how their side had managed to lose in Glasgow.

Broadcaster Onur Yildiz absolutely savaged Martin O’Neill’s side and claimed they wouldn’t even finish in the TOP TEN in Turkey. And former Besiktas star Nihat Kahveci was hardly more complimentary, branding Celtic’s first-half display the worst he had ever seen from the Hoops and wondering how Besiktas possibly managed to turn such a comfortable night into defeat.

The Istanbul giants arrived in Glasgow unbeaten in the League Phase after a testing opening trio against Marseille, Hoffenheim and Crystal Palace. And for 45 minutes, they appeared to be cruising towards another positive result as Celtic struggled to lay a glove on them.

But the game was transformed after the break. The Hoops cranked up the tempo and deservedly came out on top to spark a furious post-mortem back in Turkey.

Read more: After missing out on another senior call-up, my Celtic form has been rewarded

And Yildiz led the inquest with an extraordinary rant which somehow stretched from Ottoman history to Vaclav Cerny’s infamous water bottle incident at Celtic Park.

Speaking on BTV, Yildiz fumed: “Samet, look. If Celtic played in our league, the Super Lig, and finished in the top ten, I’ll change my name.

“Look, Besiktas played against such a bad team today. During the first half, Nubel almost got pneumonia. The ball didn’t reach the man.

“So you take the lead in the second half. You’re saying it’s going to be like a tourist trip. A match you’ll win, and you’ll go home happy and cheerful. It’s like a friendly in an Austrian training camp.

“But something happens to Besiktas away from home, and suddenly the fans start tearing their hair out. Look. Corum, Kocaelispor, Kasimpasa. I dare say these are way, way better teams than Celtic.

“The guys came with a 0-3 record. They were coming to get their first point from us. They got their first win against us. So Besiktas played against such a bad team. It’s time we started talking about the shortcomings.

“So it’s over for Besiktas. The Tulip Period is over. First of all, Besiktas absolutely needed to sign a good central defender. The defence is falling apart. At the start of the season, Haric was the only kid who resisted. Apart from Emirhan, the defence is bad. Djalo is bad. Agbadou is bad. Besiktas conceded their first goal because of him.

“We were shouting from the rooftops that they needed a right-winger. There’s no right-winger either. Why did they keep Cerny on today? How did he last so long? He gets a bit more motivated in this game because of some past incidents.

“There’s an incident, I don’t know if you remember, Cerny was playing for Glasgow Rangers. Glasgow Rangers score a goal against Celtic, Cerny pulled a water bottle from the bench and sprayed it at the Celtic fans. That’s why he was booed every time the ball came to his feet.

“He was booed not only because he played for Rangers, but also because of that incident. But Besiktas’ flaws have now been revealed.”

Before joining AC Milan, Mario Gila was already seen as one of the best defenders in Italy. Now, it has only become clearer.

There is a genuine case to be made that Gila is Milan’s best player. The Spaniard has made a significant impact on the backline, both defensively and offensively. As good a defender as he is an outlet, it appears the Rossoneri have struck gold.

In the summer, it seemed like the price paid was something of a bargain, now that has only been reaffirmed. He’s quickly become a core part of the defence and only injuries have stopped him from being the first name on the teamsheet.

Queste le sue parole raccolte da Tuttoavellino.it: "Siamo partiti bene, abbiamo avuto diverse occasioni per fare gol. #2210. Data estimates how much Cardiff City star Jack Moylan is worth ahead of potential January interest

Cardiff City have made a respectable start to life back in the Championship, although Brian Barry-Murphy’s side have struggled to find consistency in front of goal. Their problems in the final third have arguably left them lower down the table than their overall performances deserve.

However, those struggles have not affected summer recruit Jack Moylan. The Bluebirds decision to bring the attacking midfielder in from Lincoln City is already looking like an excellent piece of business.

The 25-year-old has quickly established himself as one of the Bluebirds’ most influential players, registering nine goals and three assists in his opening 14 Championship appearances. Moylan has also started every league fixture, highlighting just how important he has become to Barry-Murphy’s plans.

With Cardiff struggling towards the lower end of the table, his contributions have been particularly valuable. If he continues producing at this level, the Bluebirds may have to contend with growing interest in their summer signing when the January transfer window opens.

While the fee was reported as undisclosed upon Moylan’s announcement, reports have suggested that Cardiff City was an initial £3m which could rise to £5m.

The Bluebirds have tied Moylan down to a four-year deal running until the summer of 2028. With that in mind, if interest does arrive in January, they are in a strong position to ask for a hefty fee and profit.

However, the data suggests that Cardiff City may have overpaid to bring Moylan in this summer, which does not bode well for a potential sale. FootballTransfers’ estimated transfer value has the attacking-midfielder’s value at €2.2m, which is around £1.8m.

Off the current Cardiff City squad, Moylan has the second highest value with only Yousef Salech higher (€3.8m). Moylan’s value is also considerably lower than the only player who has more Championship goals then him Will Lankshear, who is valued at €20.7m.

A more direct comparison may be Blackburn Rovers striker Andri Gudjohnsen, who also has nine goals this campaign. His value is only €2.7m and much similar to Moylan’s, while being just a year younger.

Moylan’s statistics underline just how influential he has become for Cardiff City. His attacking numbers are particularly impressive, with 51 shots, 19 on target and 18 chances created.

He has also registered five big chances created, while his nine goals have come from an expected goals figure of 5.48, highlighting his clinical finishing and ability to outperform the underlying numbers.

The Irishman has delivered in some of Cardiff’s biggest performances, scoring twice in their 5-1 victory over Watford while impressing in a central striking role. He also scored a first-half hat-trick in the 3-3 draw with West Ham during the week.

Having progressed from Irish football to becoming a key figure in Lincoln’s League One title-winning campaign, Moylan has adapted impressively to the Championship.

#2209. RILEGGI IL LIVE – Under 18, Napoli-Juventus 1-1 (3′ De Rosa, 43′ Santa Maria). Il Napoli non sfonda il muro Juve

91′- Occasione Napoli, tiro a giro di D’Angelo, palla a lato di poco.

88′ – Occasione sprecata per la Juve, Aresini dribbla un difensore azzurro dalla sinistra ma si fa rimpallare il tiro.

77′ – Triplo cambio Juve, fuori Baba Hay, Yeboah e Paonessa, dentro Basile, Urbano e Aresini.

75′ – Occasione Napoli, palla al limite dell’area di rigore, tiro potente e preciso di Sicignano, palla di pochissimo alta.

72′ – Cambi Napoli: fuori Pengue e Lanese, dentro D’Angelo e Sicignano.

68′ – Stacca di testa Piccolo sugli sviluppi di un angolo, palla alta di poco.

67′ – Cambi Juve: Fuori Marchisio e Santa Maria, dentro Gianbavicchio e Aresini.

66′ – Occasione Napoli, ancora Pengue a inventare sulla sinistra, dribbla un paio di calciatori, serve a rimorchio, tiro di De Rosa smorzato dalla difesa e parata semplice per Giaretta.

60′ – Cambi Napoli: Fuori Lepre e Postiglione, dentro Pane e Piccolo.

57′ – Due cambi per la Juve: fuori Rogoz e Carfora, dentro Michelis e Del Fabro.

43′ – PAREGGIO JUVE, punizione di Brancato dal lato destro, che trova sul secondo palo una sponda perfetta, palla rimessa in mezzo per Santa Maria che deve solo appoggiarla in porta. 1-1.

38′ – Ancora Napoli in attacco, ottima parata di Giaretta su Ascione.

37′ – Traversa Napoli con Postiglione che prova un pallonetto da lontanissimo.

34′ – RIGORE FALLITO DA PAONESSA, PALO PIENO.

34′ RIGORE JUVE. Abbattuto Paonessa in area di rigore. Il numero 9 aveva già calciato in porta, ma per l’arbitro è rigore.

29′ – OCCASIONE NAPOLI. Lancio lungo dalle retrovie per Pengue che lotta spalla a spalla con il difensore, tiro di destro parato da Giaretta.

25′ – OCCASIONISSIMA JUVE. Passaggio filtrante dalla retrovie, Paonessa viene perso dalla difesa e a tu per tu col portiere fallisce, grande parata di Amendola che lo ferma con i piedi.

23′ – Palla persa dalla Juventus in fase di costruzione, recupera Brancato che calcia col sinistro di poco a lato.

15′ – Napoli ancora pericoloso con l’accoppiata Pengue-De Rosa, cross dalla sinistra, colpo di testa debole e controllo semplice per il portiere della Juve Giaretta.

7′ – Si vede la Juventus in attacco. Cross a campanile di Yeboah che trova Paonessa. L’attaccante prova una rovesciata acrobatica, ma la palla termina alta sopra la traversa.

3′ – VANTAGGIO NAPOLI! Percussione sulla sinistra di Pengue che rientra e mette la palla al centro, arriva De Rosa a rimorchio che stoppa il pallone e segna di destro. 1-0!

10.31 – PARTITA INIZIATA, CALCIO D’INIZIO JUVENTUS

SSC NAPOLI: Amendola, Maione, Chiaiese, Russo, Lepre, Napoletano, Pengue (VK), Lanese, Ascione, Postiglione, De Rosa (K). A disposizione: Capasso, Iammarino, Coppola, Pane, Esposito, Auxilia, Sicignano, D’Angelo D., Piccolo. Allenatore: Polise F.

JUVENTUS: Giaretta, Rogoz, Carfora, Bocchetti, Baba Hay, Lacmanovic, Yeboah, Marchisio, Paonessa, Brancato, Santa Maria. A disposizione: Rostagno, Gatti, Michelis, Del Fabro, Basile, Gianbavicchio, Urbano, Bolongo, Aresini. Allenatoe: Panzanaro P.

ASSISTENTE 1: Mario Cammarota (Nola). ASSISTENTE 2: Vincenzo Ferrara (Castellammare di Stabia).

Benvenuti alla diretta testuale di IamNaples.it di Napoli-Juventus, gara valida per la decima giornata del campionato Under 18. Gli azzurrini sono a tre punti dalla zona play-off, l’ultima posizione utile è del Genoa in questo momento storico. La Juventus è quinta in classifica, con cinque lunghezze di vantaggio sul Napoli che nell’ultimo turno ha perso 3-2 sul campo della capolista Atalanta; i bianconeri, invece, hanno battuto 3-2 il Como.

#2208. Bayern, Hoeness preoccupato per Musiala: "Non sappiamo se tornerà mai quello di prima"

Cresce la preoccupazione in casa Bayern Monaco per le condizioni di Jamal Musiala. Il talento tedesco, alle prese con problemi di salute che ne hanno condizionato la disponibilità, ha ripreso ad allenarsi con il gruppo e potrebbe tornare a disposizione dopo la sosta per le nazionali. A sollevare interrogativi sul suo recupero completo è stato però Uli Hoeness, presidente onorario del club bavarese, intervenuto ai microfoni della televisione pubblica BR. Le sue dichiarazioni lasciano emergere tutta l'incertezza sul futuro del centrocampista offensivo, che nel febbraio 2025 ha rinnovato il contratto fino al 2030, con un ingaggio di circa 25 milioni di euro a stagione.

Il dirigente ha parlato apertamente della situazione del nazionale tedesco, che secondo quanto riportato soffre di un disturbo neurologico funzionale con crisi di assenza: "Si trova in una situazione complicata: ha una malattia non facilmente curabile, ma che può essere tenuta sotto controllo in una certa misura con i farmaci. Tuttavia, non sappiamo se tornerà mai a giocare come prima". Hoeness ha poi affrontato anche l'aspetto contrattuale: "Continua a percepire lo stipendio, ma immaginate se il Bayern mettesse in discussione il suo contratto: le sue capacità attuali non corrispondono più a quanto previsto dal contratto stesso". Parole che evidenziano i timori del dirigente, senza che vi siano certezze sull'effettiva evoluzione delle condizioni del calciatore.

Nel corso dell'intervista, Hoeness si è soffermato anche sulla situazione di Vincent Kompany, lontano dalla panchina da oltre due settimane a causa di un problema di salute legato alla meningite. "Siamo molto preoccupati, anche se non credo sia così grave. Penso si sia trattato di una brutta influenza che si è trasformata in meningite. È curabile". Il presidente onorario ha quindi sottolineato il carico di lavoro dell'allenatore belga: "È sottoposto a un forte stress. Lavora dodici ore al giorno, sei giorni alla settimana". Infine, una previsione sul rientro: "Dopo la pausa per le nazionali, tra due o tre settimane, tornerà in panchina".

#2207. Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

Spain should withdraw as co-hosts of the 2030 World Cup if Morocco is awarded the right to stage the final, the European nation’s main opposition party leader has said.

The centenary finals are set to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal, with the opening three matches due to be staged in South America as a nod to Uruguay’s hosting of the inaugural tournament in 1930.

FIFA has not confirmed which of the three main co-hosts will be awarded the final, only saying that a decision will be taken in due course.

However, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the opposition People’s Party, insists Spain should back out of hosting the tournament if it is not chosen to stage the final.

“If Morocco ends up hosting the final, Spain should leave the organisation (of the tournament),” he told El Chiringuito TV.

Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Aberdeen suffer major double blow as Stephen Robinson confirms injury lay-offs

SPFL star targets goal rush after finally breaking his Premiership duck

He added on X in a post quoting the El Chiringuito interview: “Restoring our country’s pride also means not letting anyone walk all over us.

“The World Cup final belongs to Spain. The world’s top footballing nation is not humiliated. I will defend my country’s interests. In this too.”

The revamped Bernabeu Stadium or Camp Nou would be worthy contenders to host, but Morocco are continuing to push for the Grande Stade Hassan II in Casablanca, with a projected capacity of 115,000, to stage the showpiece game.

Morocco is currently staging the Under-17 boy’s World Cup, held an emergency meeting of the FIFA management board in August when FIFA president Gianni Infantino looked under threat and will also be the venue for next year’s FIFA Congress, where Infantino is hoping to secure a fourth term as president.

#2206. Amorim discusses Milan’s consistency, identity and disappointments so far: “We can beat anyone”

Ahead of Thursday’s Europa League game against Ferencvaros, AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

Tomorrow, Milan will be forced to bounce back in Europe with three points. It’s been an up-and-down campaign for them so far, losing to Benfica and Bournemouth, but they grabbed a win against RB Salzburg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A top-eight place is not out of the question, but they will have to be perfect for all of their remaining games in the Europa League league phase. In short, it will not be easy, but it’s not impossible.

Tomorrow, the Portuguese is expected to rotate heavily, offering some of his senior players a chance to rest after a very busy October. For example, Strahinja Pavlovic didn’t train today and isn’t expected to start, either.

Speaking alongside Koni De Winter, Amorim addressed the quality of his opponents, rotations and his assessments of the season so far, as MilanNews relays.

The Derby was a good one, but now it’s behind them. Milan needs consistency…

“This is the objective. The Inter game is over and we need to focus on the Europa League. We were very consistent during the derby, but there were games where we weren’t. This is the big step forward we need to take.

“Rotation doesn’t matter, nor the players we field: we need to be a great team. We need to win tomorrow, because it’s crucial to our goal of going all the way in this competition.”

“First of all, the most important match is the next one. We have to be very careful with some players. We have this busy schedule behind us and we can’t afford to lose many players for the next matches, because sometimes, when you don’t want to rotate your squad, you end up with an injury that keeps you out for a month or a month and a half.

“This is the most important match; we’re only thinking about it, but we’ll have to rotate a bit, and all the players are ready to handle the impact of the demands of the game. We have the desire to win the match.

“We’ll be facing a great opponent who has nine points in this competition, a team that hasn’t lost a single game in the league, but our players are ready, and we have a duty to win.”

Why this difference between Serie A and the Europa League?

“But if you look at the games against Benfica, I think we didn’t play our best, despite having more possession. We had some problems with the few chances we gave the opponent, and we conceded goals.

“Then we won a great game in Salzburg and then in Bournemouth. We had a red card, two penalties, and it was our fault. Maignan’s situation didn’t help us fight for the game, and sometimes these dynamics happen at certain times.

“I think we’re not doing very well in Serie A; obviously, we won the last one, but looking at the team and the games, I think we should have more points. So I’m not satisfied in the Europa League, I’m not satisfied in Serie A.

“I think we can do better, but that’s how it goes sometimes. Every game has its own story. But I think we can do better tomorrow and win.”

“They’re a team that’s used to winning, no matter the context. It gives you full confidence in every game. They’re comfortable. They’re doing very well in the league. They play a 4-2-3-1 formation and have a strong identity.

“In midfield, Nagy is very good at building play. They’re comfortable; they come to San Siro with nothing to lose. The responsibility at San Siro is ours: we have to play well and stay focused.

“I told the players that against Inter we did well because we remained humble and attentive to detail: against Ferencvaros, we’ll have to do the same because they’re a very strong team.”

After the Europa League draw, Antonio Cassano said that Milan and Juventus cannot take victory against Ferencvaros for granted…

“Without a doubt. We’re capable of winning every match and losing every match. It depends on our approach, regardless of the opponent. Everyone knows everyone; every player has the tools to understand, and the coaches have the tools to prepare everything as best as possible.

“We can win and lose against anyone; it’s all up to us. And sometimes you also need a little bit of luck.”

Does your AC Milan already have a clear identity? Are we far off?

You often ask me when we’ll reach the top. We’ll never reach the top, even if we win every game. We always have to improve. We already have an identity: we want to dominate games, sometimes we manage to do it, sometimes we don’t.

“Sometimes we change the formation and the defensive phase and nobody even notices. Our identity is to be proactive: we still lack the ability to put opponents in the box to create more chances.

“But we’re playing better, we even manage certain moments better. But there’s still a lot of work to do, especially in the final 30 meters: I have to help my players do that.

On the excellent defensive phase against Inter:

“Inter are a thing of the past. We can show tomorrow that we can defend better. We defended, but with the ball. It allowed us to think better. Details are important: a meter is a meter. We were better than Bologna.

“We were very aggressive on the wings. Koni was exceptional, but if a cross comes in for Thuram, it’s very difficult to defend, so we were more aggressive without the ball to avoid crosses. We have to do the same tomorrow; they are used to winning games.

“When a team consistently wins, there must be a reason, and we have to be ready for tomorrow.”

“We have to give him credit; he’s working really well. He went through a period without playing and was a bit frustrated, but he’s always worked very well. I think he can play this role on the wing. We played with Moreira there once, but against Inter it was Diawara. Same role, different interpretation.

“During the break, against Padova, we tried him at left back: he showed important signs. He’s quick, he’s strong. He’s doing well, he has the potential to improve a lot. Against Inter, we knew how dangerous crosses could be, especially from Inter’s left flank.

“Dimarco didn’t play, but the tactical idea remained the same, and defending crosses with Koni and Pavlovic proved to be a good idea. They almost scored from a cross with Calhanoglu, but I think he’s doing really well.

“He has plenty of room for improvement, and who knows, maybe he’ll start tomorrow.”

“What I was saying about winning games, this is the team’s strength, our identity. I always put the team first, not the individual, even though we have excellent individual players. The Ferencvaros striker is very strong in space: he can play both as a winger and as a forward, and I think he’ll play as a striker against us.

“Nagy is an important player because he understands the game. He knows exactly when to drop back and when to stay high, and I really like that kind of player.

“Add to this the quality of the left-back with his right foot who can cut inside: all these little details define an identity that I really appreciate in this team, and we’ll have to be ready to process all this information to prepare and win the match.

“I repeat: we have three points in this competition and we absolutely must win tomorrow.”

It was the best second half of the entire championship, the one against Inter. I saw the attitude of a great team: authoritative, confident, without taking risks. Should we start again from the second half?

“I think it’s a good point. But you can’t separate the second half from the first; they’re connected. We took the lead in the first half, then we controlled the game that way in the second half. We improved our understanding of the game; we were complete in all areas.

“Maybe we were lacking in putting a few players behind Inter’s midfield: we had good possession, but we can do even better. It’s just one game, anyway. But thinking only about the derby is a small-team mentality: every game is important to us.

“Tomorrow I’ll understand my team better than the derby. I don’t care about the Inter game anymore. Was it nice to win? Yes. But I’m still angry about the Bologna game. Tomorrow we’ll have to be strong to win.”

The Derby showed a side of Cardinale emotional… When will we see her like this too?

“When we win the Scudetto or a major title, maybe I’ll be excited. Until then, it’s just another day. But I didn’t expect to feel this way during the match, and neither did Cardinale. He gave an important interview, saying he supports the coach.

“There was a wonderful feeling in the stadium; he enjoyed this moment and was emotional. He’s American, but when you spend time here, you become a little Italian. However, I won’t be excited until I win something. And when I do win something, I’ll already be thinking about the next Scudetto. I doubt you’ll see me emotional.”

I’m really starting to like Amorim interviews. It’s refreshing to hear a coach be candid and open about the club. He takes accountability and protects his players and he does hide from the responsibility

“It’s just one game, anyway. But thinking only about the derby is a small-team mentality: every game is important to us… Was it nice to win? Yes. But I’m still angry about the Bologna game. Tomorrow we’ll have to be strong to win“

#2205. Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

Thomas Tuchel says Cole Palmer is paying the price for his controversial withdrawal from England’s last camp.

The Chelsea forward was a notable omission from Tuchel’s squad for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

He was originally named in Tuchel’s group for September and October’s matches but withdrew due to a minor injury, despite playing 90 minutes in Chelsea’s final match, much to the annoyance of the German, who said he “misses too many opportunities to impress”.

The 24-year-old then featured in all four of his club’s Premier League matches ahead of this camp, but was overlooked by Tuchel, who handed maiden call-ups to Jobe Bellingham and Josh King.

“I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, and Cole is no exception,” Tuchel said.

“We’re speaking now about the player who is not in camp, and it counts when you are in camp.

“And I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp. It was two and a half weeks, and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary and that’s why the credit goes to them.

“The trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

“So it’s not personal, and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country. But the competition is on, and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.

“The door is always open, but nothing has changed, and we decided to do this camp without him.”

Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

Returning star makes 'up my game' admission amid striker battle

Aberdeen suffer major double blow as Stephen Robinson confirms injury lay-offs

Palmer was one of five withdrawals ahead of the last camp, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford also pulling out.

Rice is the only one of that quintet recalled as Tuchel reiterated that he will always give preference to those who “walk the talk”.

“The best reactions to the withdrawals in the last camp from the players who were in camp was just to put the quality in and make it a successful camp,” Tuchel said.

“That’s the best foundation for the next camp, to have less withdrawals, which is actually happening now.

“So it’s always about the ones who are in camp.

“It’s always the ones who don’t withdraw and who walk the talk and come to camp and show that it matters and put the quality in. And this is always what we will reward.

“That was always the message, very, very early, since we took charge, that it matters if you are in camp and it matters what you do in camp and the last camp was an excellent one, so the trust and the belief is in the players that were there.”

Mainoo was also overlooked, despite returning to Manchester United’s side.

“I think Kobbie had a difficult spell now with his team and his club, and missed a lot, a lot of matches,” Tuchel said.

“And in the meantime, it was Jobe who impressed in the same level of time, and that’s exactly what we want.

“The door is always open for younger ones to overtake or to make their mark.”

#2203. 19-year-old Southampton starlet showcasing exciting potential in European loan after early transfer interest

Southampton sent eight players out on loan this campaign. With a mixture of academy talents and players who are on their way out of St Mary’s, the Saints are seeing mixed success from the departed members of the squad.

Moses Sesay, Nicholas Oyekunle and Jay Robinson were the three teenagers to leave for the season. It’s the latter who Tonda Eckert will be monitoring closely after a breakout term last year in the Championship.

Robinson made 28 appearances for Southampton, scoring twice and providing an assist. Minutes were always going to be hard to come by for the 19-year-old this season. With a move to Monza secured, the attacker has plenty to prove in the Serie A.

Securing a loan move to Serie A is a positive sign of how much potential Robinson has to unlock. It’s safe to say that despite a slow start to life at Monza, the 19-year-old is becoming a key player for the Italian outfit.

The Southampton academy graduate had to wait until September to make his first start, and he impressed in a 1-0 win against Torino. Featuring in an attacking midfield role, he completed the most dribbles in the game with four and had nine touches inside the opposition’s box.

His first goal came in the next match, in which he completed 78% of his passes and was dispossessed only once. Former Saints boss Ivan Juric has shown full faith in Robinson, starting the teenager in three of the last four outings.

The 19-year-old’s best display came against Cagliari, where he scored once in a 4-0 win. Two out of his three dribbles were successful in the game, and he made three line-breaking passes. It has been an impressive loan stint for the youngster with Inter Milan registering their interest.

Southampton have the option to recall Robinson from his loan spell in January. However, given his promising spell so far, the Saints would be reckless to do so.

At left-wing, the South Coast outfit currently have the options of Leo Scienza and Sam Edozie, as well as Lewis Dobbin, who can play there too. Edozie is likely to depart in January, though, after putting in a transfer request late in the summer window.

This would ultimately leave Eckert’s side short of attackers in that position. However, they must avoid recalling Robinson to improve their depth. Even if Edozie were to leave, his exit would give Dobbin a better chance of breaking into the first team after just 409 minutes played.

Most importantly, it would do no favours to the 19-year-old’s development. The Southampton prospect has only recently become settled at Monza, and with his minutes increasing over the last couple of months, the South Coast outfit can’t afford to ruin his crucial playing time.

#2201. De Winter discusses clean sheet chances, relationship with Pavlovic and starting role: “I feel good”

Today, Koni De Winter sat alongside Ruben Amorim for a press conference ahead of AC Milan vs. Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

It’s been a big year for De Winter, with the Belgian going from strength to strength. After the Supercoppa Italiana game against Napoli, the defender has seemingly improved constantly,  even becoming something of a regular for Massimiliano Allegri towards the tail end of last season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, Ruben Amorim has relied on him this season. So far, he’s played in every game of the campaign, and whilst the defence has been hampered by injuries around him, he’s been an ever-present option for the Portuguese.

After the birth of his child today, he was celebrated by the team at Milanello, and he will hope to make a strong week – after the derby win, too – an even better one, with a win tomorrow.

Speaking alongside Amorim, De Winter answered several questions from the media, as MilanNews relays.

This year you became a regular for AC Milan and now you’ve also become a father…

“Becoming a dad is a wonderful thing. On the pitch, I feel more important than last year and I feel more confident. I think it’s a great moment, but there’s still a long way to go.”

You’ve played pretty much all the time so far. Did you expect that?

“I feel good. When there are a lot of games, you train by playing. For me, it’s better this way. So for me, it’s fine like this; I have to be ready.”

You almost always play alongside Pavlovic. How do you get along with the Serbian?

“I feel good with all my teammates; we know each other well. I like playing with Pavlovic; he’s strong and we understand each other very well.”

How difficult will it be to keep a clean sheet tomorrow?

“They’re a good team, they’re having a good Europa League, they have great confidence, but we’ll do our best to stop them from scoring.”

Milan has had many great defenders. Do you have any role models?

“I have several. If I have to name one who played for AC Milan, I’d say Thiago Silva, whom I followed a lot and who is very good. If I have to name one, I’d say his.”

“As the coach says, he’s someone who works hard and always gives his all. Everyone loves him. When you work hard, your chance comes, and he grabbed it with both hands. We’re all happy for him.”

#2200. Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team

Neil McCann will continue his drive to see Kilmarnock “flourish” in the face of growing fan scrutiny.

The Ayrshire club are one point ahead of William Hill Premiership bottom side Hibernian, with nine points from 36 and having conceded 28 goals from 12 games amid concern and disgruntlement among a section of the Killie support.

McCann is preparing his players to take on a Celtic team who are four points ahead of Rangers at the top of the table, having played a game more and on the back of a morale-boosting 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas on Thursday night

However, the Kilmarnock boss remains positive, and said: “Supporters will always give their opinion when they come into the stadium and they’ll voice it. They’re entitled to voice their opinion.

“My pressure, to be honest with you, is preparing our players tactically, physically, mentally.

Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission Spain told to walk away from 2030 World Cup if Morocco gets final

“And then when they take the field, I give them full autonomy to go and carry out all of those instructions, but play with the freedom and bravery that got us out of trouble last year.

“Nothing’s changed in my build-up. Nothing’s changed in my drive. Nothing’s changed in my approach to getting Kilmarnock to be a team that wants to put on a product on the pitch.

“A lot’s been made of ‘you can just win games and it’s all about winning games’. And I absolutely get that when it comes to management.

“Of course, it’s about results, very much, it’s a results-driven business. But I was given this job to get us out of bother last year.

“And we came in, the first thing wasn’t about, yes, results were important, but it was making sure that the team were capable and prepared to go and get those results.

“I think we are prepared to go and get those results. We just haven’t given our support enough good days to celebrate wins.

“But the work doesn’t stop. And it doesn’t deter me one bit from the work that I do on the training field.

“I’ll hopefully see a team flourish, get the results that I think their performances deserve. And then we can all come together with the unity that we showed last season and hopefully Kilmarnock will start climbing the table.”

#2198. Sheffield Wednesday team news and predicted XI as Dave Challinor takes charge vs Oldham Athletic

Sheffield Wednesday travel to the North West for their first game under Dave Challinor‘s management. An FA Cup first round clash against Oldham Athletic awaits SWFC, and the new boss will be eager to make a winning start.

Challinor is tasked with turning around some poor form of late as the Owls have gone four without a win, including consecutive draws under Matt Hamshaw’s temporary lead. Wednesday have a good history in this prestigious competition though, with 2021/22 the last time they got knocked out in the first round.

Oldham Athletic meanwhile sit 18th in League Two, so will be hoping for some cup joy. In their last game, Micky Mellon’s Latics won 1-0 against Northampton Town thanks to a second-half goal from Ollie Norburn.

Challinor has a handful of injury issues to deal with as he prepares to make his Sheffield Wednesday bow. Before the game, the new boss confirmed the Owls will be without Liam Cooper, Joe Lumley and Ali Al-Hamadi as their recent absences continue.

Cooper is a precautionary call, while Lumley and Al-Hamadi are expected to step up their returns next week.

Elsewhere, Billy Mitchell and Reece James are set to miss out, as are long-term absentees Louie Barry and Tyler Onynago. Sil Swinkels is suspended after his sending off against Blackpool, but Jamal Lowe will be available for selection having served his ban.

In better news, Di’Shon Bernard has been deemed fit to return for SWFC. Challinor is wary that his minutes still need to be managed but the former Manchester United youngster’s availability serves as a welcome boost.

Centre-back Ricardo Santos returned off the bench against Blackpool and is set to be in contention again.

Maynard-Brewer; Bernard, Santos, Weaver; Valery, Heskey, Bannan, Lowe; Slattery, Keillor-Dunn; Burstow

Challinor has mainly played with a 3-4-2-1 in his managerial career to date, so that is what formation is anticipated in his first Sheffield Wednesday game. However, he has used varied three-back setups as well as a 4-2-3-1 in the past.

Lumley’s absence means Ashley Maynard-Brewer continues in goal. He will be guarded by Ernie Weaver, and the fit-again Bernard and Santos in the back three with Yan Valery and Max Lowe selected as right and left wing-backs.

The fairly limited midfield depth means SWFC will likely persist with Barry Bannan and Jaden Heskey in the middle. Callum Slattery continues in a more advanced role alongside Davis Keillor-Dunn, who has now scored four goals in 10 games for the club.

Mason Burstow continues at striker despite Lowe’s return. The experienced striker will be hoping to impact the game off the bench though, alongside the likes of Sean Fusire, Jordi Liongola, Kieran Morrison and Harry Gray.

Oldham Athletic vs Sheffield Wednesday kicks off at 17:15 on Sunday evening and will be broadcast on TNT Sports 1.

#2196. Ex-Celtic star tells Martin O'Neill why he's on receiving end of 'flak with love'

Joe Hart has told Martin O'Neill why he is getting "flak with love" amid Celtic's stuttering form.

Scrutiny at the club is growing and growing after a draw with Dundee United was followed up by defeat to Falkirk. Previously, the domestic form had been almost flawless, but for losing to Rangers.

Fans are now concerned their lead at the top of the table is precarious and are questioning the direction of the club even more.

Former Parkhead goalkeeper Hart says that scrutiny is always going to be there and it does not affect O'Neill's standing with the support.

He told The Overlap: "It’s flak with love, and that doesn’t make any sense. Of course, we know it doesn’t make any sense, but Martin O’Neill will be, and is, absolutely adored. But he knows what he signed up for as a Celtic manager, and he would expect to be getting a lot of questions asked about him.

Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

And that’s not saying he’s not up to the task or he’s not the man for the job, but that’s what comes with the territory. If you really understand Celtic, you understand that if you’re not borderline perfect domestically and challenging in Europe, you’re going to get it.

"You’re going to get it because they care and they’re intelligent football fans. And, there’s a massive disharmony with the board. The fans really don’t understand what the direction of the club is. And obviously the board have got their opinions in terms of the success that they had and continue to have.

So, it is difficult. That was really shining brightly mid-season last season, but then Martin came back in and the team started to win and it goes away. It’s amazing what winning can do, and at the moment they’re not.

"They had a difficult result at Falkirk. I think they drew at home to Dundee United. And then this Besiktas game felt ominous. It felt like there was going to be a riot, or not even a riot. Do you know what the worst feeling you can have in a stadium is? And I very rarely felt it up there. It wasn’t anger, it was people going, ‘Pfft, we lost again.’ That is the worst feeling you could have.

"You’d rather have someone that impassioned, that embroiled as a Celtic fan. Like I say, domestically, I lost very, very few games, but no matter what run you’d been on, you could feel it. It wasn’t the majority, but you’d feel some people’s whole life and whole livelihood is proudly Celtic.

"And if you don’t perform in that shirt, you’re going to get it. I’ve still got friends up there, and they were flat going into the game. If Celtic had lost, they wouldn’t have been angry, they’d have been like, ‘Oh, God.’ And that’s not a nice feeling. I talked about it for Michael [Carrick], but I think it’s a little bit different up there, because they’re still top of the league.

"If they can take the atmosphere that they generated towards the end of the game last night into the league game this weekend, I think it’s Kilmarnock, then it could be a massive spark to go again.”

#2193. Blackburn Rovers defender has had an excellent breakout year – but patience is required: Opinion

Blackburn Rovers have had a largely frustrating 2026, but there has been reason to believe. The return of Tony Mowbray has seen the club build on Michael O’Neill’s work and pushed the club up into mid-table.

Another huge positive over the last year has been the emergence of Tom Atcheson. The 20-year-old becoming one of Rovers’ most encouraging academy success stories, with his development over the past 12 months earning him recognition on the international stage.

His form has also attracted attention from several top clubs. Atcheson was the subject of enquiries from Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Crystal Palace in the summer window.

The 20-year-old has progressed from a promising youngster to a regular Championship starter and an increasingly important member of Northern Ireland’s defence. His senior breakthrough has not simply been a reward for potential, either.

Consistent performances at club level have given O’Neill plenty of reasons to trust him, with Atcheson starting all four of Northern Ireland’s Nations League fixtures in September and October, helping them record a run of clean sheets.

That is a significant achievement for a player who only made his senior international debut in March. Having joined Blackburn at under-12 level, Atcheson enjoyed a loan spell with Marine before making his Championship debut against Millwall in December 2025.

14 league appearances followed last season, and he has since established himself as a regular under Tony Mowbray.

Atcheson’s underlying numbers this campaign suggest there is plenty to like, although they also highlight why expectations should remain measured. His average FotMob rating of 6.54 also indicates that, despite his impressive international progress, he has not consistently been among the Championship’s standout defenders.

There have been occasional reminders of his inexperience, too. His first international start against Guinea in June ended with a goal and a red card, while a difficult 45 minutes against Swansea last month preceded a minor groin problem that forced him to miss the subsequent Stoke fixture.

Nevertheless, Blackburn have every reason to be encouraged. Atcheson has already demonstrated that he can translate Championship reliability into international performances, and his physical profile makes him an appealing long-term prospect.

The Premier League comparisons may be premature, but his trajectory is undeniably positive. Another six to 12 months of consistent performances could take his reputation, and his market value, to another level.

#2192. Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to

Mika Baur is enjoying the demands of being a Celtic player – and was delighted to see the team display their fighting spirit and belief as they broke their Europa League duck.

The 22-year-old impressed as Celtic came from behind to beat Besiktas 3-2 on Thursday and get off the mark in the Europa League at the fourth time of asking.

The Hoops were heading for a seventh defeat in 11 matches when they fell behind early in the second half but the introduction of Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Colby Donovan on the hour mark sparked the team into life.

Manager Martin O’Neill recently admitted that some new players were still adapting to the demands of playing for Celtic but Baur and Duran have quickly proved they were successful summer signings.

Baur arrived from Paderborn after helping them to promotion to the Bundesliga and made his Germany debut last month, but moving to Scotland has been a new experience.

Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team Cole Palmer pays England price as Thomas Tuchel explains ruthless omission

“To play every three days is different for me,” the midfielder said. “I think I have played the same amount of games now that I had last season by the winter break.

“But I like it. That’s what you want. You want to play all the time, more playing than training. I am really enjoying it.

“And I think the pressure to win is a good kind of pressure. It’s better than (trying) not to lose. So I really enjoy it.”

Baur has shown pace and skill on the ball but his pressing in the final stages drew massive appreciation from the crowd on Thursday.

“First of all, I want to work hard for the team, for myself, that I can prove myself and I can play on the stage, help the team, put in a shift, hard work,” he said.

“That’s what I have to do first. And then after this, the skill comes, playing with the ball. But first of all, it’s showing heart on the field. I was really happy that it was appreciated.”

The win over the Turkish side felt like it could be a major step in Celtic’s season as they bounced back from losing the opening goal and from a late equaliser, with Duran netting the winner seconds later.

“The second half was pure heart, pure fight,” Baur said. “I’m not here for a long time, but I think that’s what it’s all about. This win feels unbelievable because we deserved it. We fought for it.

“The team is really, really close together. We know that we had a tough couple of weeks, but you can feel it in the training sessions, how the team is working together, the feeling, the believing is always there. And it was there on the pitch. That’s what we have to show week by week, every three days.

“It was not just our win. The atmosphere was great. I’m really, really thankful for every supporter in the stadium. They gave us a lot of energy. We all fight together. That makes me happy.”

#2191. Cina, che crollo del Chengdu: perde 12 punti in 4 giornate e regala il titolo al Dalian Yingbo

Una delle rimonte più incredibili degli ultimi anni si è consumata nel campionato cinese, dove il Chengdu Rongcheng ha gettato alle ortiche un titolo che sembrava ormai conquistato. A quattro giornate dalla conclusione, la formazione allenata da John Aloisi vantava addirittura 12 punti di vantaggio sulla più immediata inseguitrice. Sarebbe bastato un solo punto nelle ultime quattro partite per festeggiare il trionfo, ma è arrivato un crollo tanto improvviso quanto inspiegabile: quattro sconfitte consecutive e primato sfumato proprio all'ultima giornata. Ad approfittarne è stato il Dalian Yingbo, protagonista di una rimonta che resterà nella storia del calcio cinese.

Il verdetto definitivo è arrivato nell'ultimo turno, quando il Chengdu è stato sconfitto per 3-2 dallo Shandong Taishan. Un risultato che ha aperto definitivamente le porte al sorpasso del Dalian, vittorioso per 3-1 contro il Tianjin. Per la formazione di Aloisi è stata la quarta sconfitta consecutiva, mentre i rivali hanno centrato il quinto successo di fila, completando una rimonta che fino a poche settimane prima sembrava impossibile. Le due squadre hanno così concluso il campionato appaiate a quota 52 punti.

A determinare l'assegnazione del titolo sono stati gli scontri diretti, entrambi vinti dal Dalian Yingbo, che ha potuto così festeggiare il primo campionato della propria storia. Un'impresa straordinaria, costruita attraverso un finale di stagione perfetto e favorita dal tracollo della capolista. Per il Chengdu Rongcheng resta invece una delusione difficilmente cancellabile: perdere un campionato con dodici punti di margine a quattro giornate dal termine, senza riuscire a conquistare neppure un pareggio, rappresenta un epilogo destinato a essere ricordato a lungo.

#2189. What Alex Neil must learn from Millwall’s 3-0 defeat to West Brom heading into the international break

Millwall have had a terrible opening third of the 2026/27 season. The Lions suffered their seventh loss of the campaign and their second this week as West Brom were 3-0 victors at The Hawthorns on Saturday.

Alex Neil’s side did well to nullify a WBA side who were unbeaten in five before the weekend inside the first 45 minutes. However, the second half saw the South London outfit capitulate defensively as they made it 27 goals conceded this term.

Millwall will welcome the pause in Championship action for two weeks as they reset. There are certainly many lessons learned from their latest defeat that the Lions must use as fuel over the international break to come back stronger heading into the busy winter period.

This time last year, when Millwall headed into the international break, they were sat 6th in the table and just four points off the top two. Now after their second consecutive 3-0 loss, the Lions are 16th in the Championship and six points from the top eight.

Neil’s side have scored six more goals than they did this time last season. However, they have conceded seven more times. Saturday highlighted the gulf in quality and momentum between a side in real play-off contention like West Brom and a team in disarray like Millwall.

The Baggies had an xG of 2.98 whereas the South London outfit only had an xG of 0.62. The Lions also had just nine touches inside the opposition’s box and won just 48% of their ground duels.

All three goals Millwall conceded against West Brom weren’t entirely at the fault of the New Zealand international. However, it’s safe to say that the Lions won’t achieve anything this season with him as their number one.

Max Crocombe has conceded 22 goals this term out of 10 games and has a save percentage of 55.1%. He is currently averaging 2.2 goals conceded per match, and the 33-year-old is struggling to cope with the demands of the Championship.

Against WBA, the New Zealand international made an error leading to a goal and made just three saves. With Lukas Jensen reported to be nearing a return to fitness and his save percentage standing at 100% from his two games this term, Neil won’t select Crocombe again if he doesn’t have to.

One positive Millwall can take from the clash against West Brom is the return of duo Josh Coburn and Tairyk Arconte. Coburn played 54 minutes before being substituted, whilst Arconte featured for the last 10 minutes.

Both players have been crucial to the limited success Neil’s side has had this season. Coburn especially had a strong start to the term before an injury sidelined him for two months. He has won 69.2% of his aerial duels this campaign and has an xG on target of 3.14.

Arconte was also missed by the Lions. He has netted three times in nine games for Millwall in his debut Championship season. The 22-year-old has a successful dribble rate of 60% and has made 45 touches inside the opposition box.

#2188. It pushes you forward – Jacob Murrell feeling fuelled by Falkirk fan fervour

Falkirk striker Jacob Murrell believes the passion of Scottish football is fuelling his goalscoring form.

The American has netted five goals since joining from DC United, helping the Bairns go on a four-game winning run ahead of Sunday’s trip to face Hearts.

The 22-year-old said: “It’s a little different just because the games matter a bit more here than they did back in the MLS, just because of the promotion/relegation and how much the fans care about results. So the intensity of the games is much higher, you’re not finding easy games.

“For me, it’s the best thing in the world to play under this type of pressure. It just gives me a purpose, it gives me that fuel.

“I love that aspect of it. I love that the way that our group goes on the field and performs matters to people. That’s the most special thing about what we get to do and it drives us on the hard days when we have to come to training, when we’re tired, when we’re sore.

Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to Neil McCann: Why nothing has changed in my approach to build strong Kilmarnock team

"We’re playing for something more than ourselves, that pushes you forward.

“Like after the Celtic match, when all the fans stayed in their seats, celebrated the win with us after, that wasn’t just a win for us as a team, but for the full club, for the fans, for the community. It was a really great moment for everybody.”

Murrell was among 17 summer signings but manager John McGlynn has quickly fashioned the group into an effective team.

“The people have been really good to me,” he said. “Falkirk in general has been really good to me. The club, the team-mates, but then the fans as well have been really good.

“There’s a bit of learning curve the first month to get up to speed and get all the stuff sorted with a car, an apartment and a bank account. All the stuff that you don’t see behind the scenes.

“Little stuff that’s different, like when I went to the grocery store, I couldn’t find eggs. Back home, they’re only in the fridge. They’re on the shelf here.

“But I’ve got into a really good rhythm with a couple of team-mates going to the gym after training and just getting into good habits where we’re cooking our own food and eating well.

“Just feeling full of confidence that we’re putting in the work and we’re going to reap the benefits of it.”

#2187. Opposition insight for Milan-Ferencvaros: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

On Thursday evening, Ferencvaros will travel to San Siro to face AC Milan in the Europa League, in a must-win game for the Rossoneri.

It’s already at that stage for Milan; if they want to qualify for the Round of 16 automatically, they must beat everyone in front of them. With three points from nine available, Ruben Amorim expressed his frustrations with this season so far, and they need to prove themselves tomorrow.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

➤ Manager: Balazs Borbely ➤ Form (all comps): D-W-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Europa League): Kristoffer Zachariassen – 5 ➤ Most assists (Europa League): Yusuf Bamidele & Veljko Birmančević – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bero, Otvos.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

#2186. Premier League club tracking Middlesbrough star Will Lankshear amid historic form

Middlesbrough only signed Will Lankshear in the summer, but the striker’s stunning form has brought excitement over his next steps. England boss Thomas Tuchel has eyes on the Boro star, and now, The Sun states Newcastle United are closely watching his performances.

Scouts were set to watch Lankshear in action against Wrexham on Wednesday, but injury kept him sidelined for that game and the 0-0 draw at Watford on Saturday. Kim Hellberg‘s side failed to score in both games, highlighting how much they are missing their star striker.

Lankshear has 13 goals in 13 Championship games, and 15 goals in 16 matches for the Teesside outfit across all competitions. No Boro player has started a season in such prolific form since club record goalscorer George Camsell in 1926.

Lankshear has been viewed as an exciting prospect for some time. Spurs snapped him up from the Sheffield United academy at a youth age and he really announced himself on the senior stage on loan at Oxford United, where he scored 12 goals and provided three assists in 47 games across the 2025/26 season.

Despite such success and encouragement over his future, there were eyebrows raised when Middlesbrough struck a deal worth £20m with add-ons to sign him in the summer. However, Lankshear has already justified the hefty fee.

Lankshear has scored four Championship braces on his way to the top of the goalscoring charts. He was on a run of seven goals in five games before injury hit and ruled him out of Boro’s last two matches.

The 21-year-old’s lethal finishing and trajectory have drawn early comparisons to England captain and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. Lankshear is currently averaging a goal every 78 minutes for Middlesbrough, so it is little surprise to see the England national team and Premier League club Newcastle United tracking his performances.

They will not be the only ones with eyes on Lankshear, who is viewed as one of the country’s most promising young attackers.

Lankshear only moved in the summer and is under contract until 2031. It means Boro aren’t under pressure to cash in.

However, to keep him long term, if Middlesbrough are to have a chance of fending off top interest, they have to ensure their trajectory matches that of Lankshear. The only way to do so is by winning promotion to the Premier League this season.

If not, there will be no shortage of clubs ready to spend big on bringing him in. Newcastle United are the only concretely reported admirer at present, but he is sure to have alerted more sides.

Middlesbrough sit 2nd in the Championship table, despite failing to win either of their last two games.

#2185. Footy Headlines: ‘An unexpected blend’ – Puma to end Milan kit run with ‘streetwear’ third shirt

Today, some news has emerged about AC Milan’s possible new third shirt for the 2027-28 season and the colours it’ll be.

The big kit news today has been the move to Adidas and how much Milan will pocket from it. After signing with Puma on a deal worth €16 million per season, they renewed on a €30m per season deal for the ‘second half’ of their relationship.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, Adidas will now blow this figure out of the park, with a €500m agreement over a 10-year period. A substantial increase, especially when paired with the stadium figures.

According to Footy Headlines, the third kit will feature an ‘unexpected blend’ of colours, with a ‘Dark Umber’ and ‘Court Grey’ design. The former is an almost-black, brownish colour, whilst the latter is a ‘mid-tone’.

To contrast this, the detailing on the shirt will be ‘vibrantly’ red, to ensure it still stands out. A kit with another ‘streetwear’-y feel to it, it will try to merge with a sophisticated look, too.

Of course, this will also be the final ‘traditional’ kit produced by the brand – in terms of a home, away and alternative shirt – and it almost reflects the end of the partnership. Based on the initial leaks of the home and away shirts, it seems like a nice mix of shirts to see off the brand’s relationship.

#2184. Marink Reedijk lays down Aberdeen challenge to Hibs team after Hearts win

Hibernian manager Marink Reedijk has challenged his players to replicate their Hampden hunger against Aberdeen as they get back in the “rat race”.

Reedijk told his players “I want music, I want beer, I want everything” when they returned to the dressing room after beating Hearts in the Premier Sport Cup semi-finals and joined in a rendition of Sunshine on Leith with their fans.

But the Dutchman is now determined to secure a first William Hill Premiership win when Hibs travel to Pittodrie.

“It was a very beautiful moment,” he said. “After the match, you saw what it meant to the fans, what it meant to the club and what it meant to the players. That is important because this is what football is about.

“The best thing for me was that we showed we can get a result in the way we want to play. We can come back from 1-0 down, play beautiful football but also do the dirty work. That was important to see.

It pushes you forward – Jacob Murrell feeling fuelled by Falkirk fan fervour Mika Baur identifies the Celtic challenge he is ready to rise to

“However, it’s history now. We need to make sure we can do it over multiple matches and for a longer period of time.

“If you achieve something as we did on Sunday, it’s important to celebrate it. We work hard, so you can also party for an evening. Then, from that point, we need to focus on Aberdeen.

“We’re in a sort of rat race, with game after game after game. We do everything at the highest possible intensity, from training sessions to matches. Therefore, you need to celebrate your victories sometimes.”

He added: “For me, it’s important that we make another step in the way we want to play. We need to do things better than we did in the last match. Whether it’s Hearts or someone else, we need to have the same hunger for every match.”
