#2183. Romano assesses ‘perfect’ derby win, the restart and Milan’s mercato targets: “A busy January”

Today, Fabrizio Romano has taken an in-depth look at AC Milan, their big weekend result and what’s next for the club.

After the Derby della Madonnina, there’s a very strong feeling surrounding Milan. All of a sudden, talk of winning a Scudetto under Ruben Amorim has gained genuine traction, and the group looks closer than ever.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s not going to be easy, of course, but the Portuguese is obsessed with the idea of lifting the Serie A trophy with the Rossoneri, referencing as much in his press conference earlier today.

If that is going to happen this season, though, they will need to invest in January. After all, the squad remains shallow and extra support is very much needed.

Speaking to Time2Play.com, Romano looked at several things, including the derby and what the next few months could look like for the Diavolo.

“A derby can change the world. Because often, dynamics are triggered on and off the pitch, the atmosphere clears in an instant, and everyone contributes.

“AC Milan knows this well: a week ago, the home defeat against Bologna had brought much criticism, though it was also clearly the result of fatigue and significant absences, given the relentless pace of matches.

“But immediately afterwards, AC Milan set up their perfect derby—on and off the pitch, it’s no small matter—to build on and not just sit back.

“Because on the pitch, from Moreira to the usual Rabiot and Ruben Amorim, defended tooth and nail by Cardinale, everyone contributed that touch that led to the three points with a ferocious approach that became a winner.

“Off the pitch, Gerry Cardinale himself left his mark. Never like this.”

“The induction of legends during the week, Ricardo Kaká in the Hall of Fame, the announcement of the new stadium alongside Inter, interviews to staunchly defend Ruben Amorim, and above all, the desire to continue improving his AC Milan 2.0 starting… in January.

“Yes, because the Rossoneri’s post-derby signals are about building, not just about exaltation. This is where we need to start again, laying the foundations for a different, fierce, and winning Milan, like the one seen in the derby, which clearly can’t be enough.”

“And the first announcement will be that of the new Head of Football: Milan has a sealed verbal agreement with Markus Krösche, the man who has done a great job at Eintracht Frankfurt in recent years, both in scouting talent and capital gains, ready to take over the Rossoneri project.

“Krösche will be active for the January transfer window and will be in direct contact with Cardinale regarding the Rossoneri’s new plans.

“He’s a figure generating enthusiasm at Casa Milan, having already been the first choice since last June: Cardinale preferred to wait a few months to have his priority rather than fall back on managers who weren’t first choices. Now, the Krösche era is about to begin.”

“Milan’s objectives? It’s going to be a busy January: the defender could and should have arrived at the end of August, but there was no timeline or method. Milan has reinstated Tomori, but at least one defensive reinforcement is already planned for January.

“The favourite since June has been Sporting’s Gonçalo Inacio, but Milan has at least three other options on the list and has recently also sent Sylla of Union St. Gilloise to scout. It might not end there: keep an eye on the attack, where an additional option to give Gonçalo Ramos a rest shouldn’t be ruled out if the right opportunity presents itself.

“Assessments about Franceso Camarda will be made in the coming weeks, but Milan is exploring the transfer market and will continue to surprise. At least one signing, likely two. And then… the transfer market will dictate inspiration, ideas, and innovations.

“With new players and a Rossoneri that has never been so fired up in recent years.”

For the first time in a while, it’s a continued stream of positive news for Milan, which is only a good thing.

#2182. Sheffield United man answers question over long-term future after West Ham, QPR summer interest

Sheffield United saw Harrison Burrows endure a tougher 2025/26 season after a fantastic debut campaign in 2024/25. Rival Championship clubs were lurking in the summer in case SUFC opted to cash in on the 24-year-old, with West Ham and QPR credited with interest while Burnley saw a late bid rejected.

However, Burrows has been back in the side and back in form in recent weeks. While speaking to The Star, the former Peterborough United man was asked about his long-term future and whether he sees it with the Blades, to which he responded: “Yeah, 100%. I’m really enjoying my football here. I really enjoy being with the lads, I really enjoy the club and I really enjoy the city. So, yeah, I’m very happy.”

Burrows is currently under contract at Bramall Lane until 2028. Sheffield United are looking to tie down a number of players to new deals, and the left-back is one of them alongside Sydie Peck, Femi Seriki and Michael Cooper.

As touched on before, Burrows endured a fantastic debut year at Sheffield United. After signing from Peterborough United, he stepped up to the Championship brilliantly as he recorded six goals and six assists in 48 games for a Blades side that made the play-off final.

Form proved harder to come by last term, and Sam McCallum emerged as the first choice at left-back before injury hit. He locked down his spot in Chris Wilder’s side early on this season too, performing well while Burrows was sidelined himself.

Harrison Burrows’ Sheffield United stats (all competitions)

However, injury has cast McCallum to the treatment room once again, and Burrows has made a fine return to the team. He has started the last five Championship matches, with only Saturday’s meeting at Charlton Athletic ending in defeat.

Burrows’ form has served as a reminder of what he offers on the left, with his technical ability making him a creative asset for SUFC. There are questions over the defensive side of his game at times, but the quality he offers with the ball can see him play a highly influential role when he’s in good form.

Aged 24, Burrows is already approaching 300 career games. He played 185 times for former club Peterborough United, and Saturday’s start against Charlton Athletic marked his 101st appearance for Sheffield United.

It means he has both an excellent amount of experience and plenty of room to keep developing. Burrows spent his youth in midfield and broke into first-team football in this position too, so he still has progress to make defensively.

With improvements in this area, SUFC will have a well-rounded left-back with strong experience and leadership abilities – as shown by his past captaincy at Peterborough United.

A challenging season and summer interest brought questions over his Bramall Lane future, but Burrows can be a valuable asset in the now and future if a new long-term deal is agreed.

#2181. Celtic's 'Che Guevaras' should show their fellow fans some respect at this year's AGM

There is about as much chance of Dermot Desmond taking a seat amongst the Union Bears ultras group the next time Celtic play Rangers at Ibrox in January as there is of the billionaire Irish financier rocking up at their AGM at Parkhead next month.

Desmond, who has been the Glasgow club’s principal shareholder for more than two decades, has not attended the gathering since way back in 2006 and he is not, with disaffection about the stewardship of the Scottish champions still rife in the stands, about to break with tradition.

The greeting which chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay, interim chairman Brian Wilson and manager Martin O’Neill received from some protesters when they attended a question-and-answer session at the Greenock Supporters’ Club this week gave an indication of the sort of treatment he would receive if he did.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of the Europa League encounter with Besiktas on Thursday night, O’Neill expressed his dismay at the fact that around 25 supporters appeared wearing face coverings. “That was the saddest thing,” he said. “I would never have thought that fans would be clothed in balaclavas at a meeting.”

The frustration in the statement which the Celtic Fans Collective, an umbrella coalition of supporters’ clubs and organisations, published this week demanding that Desmond make a rare appearance at the meeting was palpable and understandable.

That the man who, rightly or wrongly but unquestionably, wields the most power at Parkhead is an annual no-show highlights everything that is wrong with how the former European Cup winners are being run. Are accountability and dialogue too much to ask for?

Is the famously publicity-shy man from Macroom in County Cork, though, really going to trap when the same individuals who hurled tennis balls at him when he was playing golf in the Alfred Dunhill Championship at St Andrews last month are likely to be in attendance?

There has been fevered speculation about when Celtic directors will face their shareholders in recent weeks. Supporters are desperate to know what their long-term football strategy is, who has been driving recruitment, how governance is going to be modernised, why tens of millions of pounds continue to sit in the bank and much else besides.

But are they likely to get answers to those questions now the AGM date has been set for Tuesday, December 1? The actions of a certain sub-section of their support in Inverclyde in midweek suggested that it could well be another bad-tempered, ugly and ultimately futile get-together.

Celtic interim chairman Brian Wilson, left, chief executive Michael Nicholson and chief financial officer Chris McKay at Parkhead (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

Ill-feeling about then-chairman Peter Lawwell bringing last year's annual meeting to a premature end amid persistent disorder still lingers. It has been suggested once again in recent days that the move was a cynical ploy by the besieged board to avoid public scrutiny.

However, David Low, the financial analyst who was a driving force behind the Fergus McCann takeover back in 1994 and is now associated with the Celtic Supporters Limited pressure group, rejected that interpretation of events when he appeared on the A Celtic State of Mind podcast last week.

“You are allowed to hold the people who shareholders elected to account once a year,” he said. “But it is a professional environment. Last year’s meeting was a bun fight. Nobody came out of that looking well. It is a professional forum and you have to respect the forum you are in.

“Give them red cards if you have to if they give an unsatisfactory answer. But listen to what is said and then react. That is the way it has always been at Celtic, even when it was a private company.

“That was a horrible meeting last year. People go there who want to learn. That is why they are there. You turn up, you ask questions and you try to learn something. If you don’t like it you can boo and do whatever within reason. But you have got to listen.

“It disintegrated into a shambles last year. It was over-the-top. There was a lot of unacceptable behaviour from the hardcore. It was not on. It was the biggest AGM in 20 years.”

There has been widespread unhappiness about the course Celtic are on for some time and a substantial section of the support wants meaningful change in how the Parkhead club is run. But some of the more vocal and militant members of the rebel alliance can be arrogant and selfish.

They did not merely show disrespect to the board last year. They showed disrespect to the hundreds of fellow shareholders who had turned up, many from far afield, wanting to exercise the same right to scrutinise those running their club.

The club later alleged that its head of safety, security and operations, Mark Hargreaves, had been threatened and intimidated by two prominent members of the Green Brigade. Whatever the truth of those allegations, it was a sorry affair from start to premature finish.

Celtic fans hold up banners referencing their teams failures against teams in Europe (Image: Andrew Milligan)

One lifelong fan voiced his exasperation at the leaders of the civil war that was raging at his beloved club in these pages as he attended the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup game against Dundee back in February.

“We don't need modern-day Che Guevaras,” he said before he ignored the boycott that had been called. “We want people who love Celtic.” He is not alone in taking that view.

The Celtic Fans Collective appealed for the “focus to be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest” at the AGM in their latest missive. They are right. The board should be made to answer searching questions. Those who shout directors down before their answers can be heard are serving neither their cause nor their fellow supporters.

It would perhaps help the Parkhead club to move forward on and off the park if those words were heeded and there were no disruptions from “aggressive and irrational factions” hellbent on “stirring up toxicity”.

#2180. Pep Guardiola and Brendan Rodgers agreed on Birmingham City star's talent

Birmingham City's impressive start to the Championship season has laid the foundations for a sustained promotion bid, some 15 years after the club last played Premier League football.

Chris Davies has endured mixed fortunes during what is still his first job in full-time management, having previously developed a strong reputation as an assistant at some of British football's biggest institutions such as Liverpool, Celtic and Tottenham Hotspur.

Having led Birmingham to their best finish in a decade after breaking several records in League One, the 41-year-old has since refined his tactical approach, and it has paid dividends, with his squad looking far more efficient all across the pitch.

In recent times, Blues have added several high-profile names to their squad, such is the backing Davies has received from Knighthead Capital Management, but it's fair to say that not all of said transfer dealings have paid off.

However, whilst his start to the current campaign has been mixed, Patrick Roberts is still seen as an integral part of the squad at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park, with the winger's technical ability being well-known for several years.

Roberts rose to initial stardom after breaking through at Fulham and for the England youth ranks, with Cottagers boss, Felix Magath, predicting a strong career for the winger.

After impressing in the Championship following the club;'s relegation in 2014, Roberts suddenly became the subject of interest from Liverpool, who were managed by Brendan Rodgers at the time.

Having made 17 appearances in the second tier, he would make a swift return to the top-flight, but with Manchester City, in a deal which had the potential to rise as high as £11m, under Manuel Pellegrini.

Roberts then made all three of his senior appearances for the North West side in a short period of time, with his debut coming in the EFL Cup against Sunderland, before Celtic struck an 18-month loan agreement for the highly-rated talent.

His impact at Parkhead was immediate, scoring six times in his first 11 appearances, before netting 11 times in 47 appearances across all competitions in 2016/17.

However, it's fair to say that his goal for the Hoops in the 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium in December 2016 raised question marks over a potential long-term future in Manchester under the legendary Pep Guardiola, who, like the aforementioned Rodgers, was in agreement over his qualities.

Jude Bellingham once named three unlikely Birmingham City players as his football heroes

“We know his quality but the decision is not about one game. It is for one season for the perspective," Guardiola stated, whilst the Northern Irishman said: "You’ve got a big English talent there and I’m sure there’s a big career for him."

Unfortunately for Roberts, his final season in Glasgow was hampered by injury, but he still won a total of seven trophies at the club before spending time on loan with Girona, Norwich City, Derby County, Middlesbrough and Troyes.

The winger then eventually settled at Sunderland, where his nine goals and 18 assists in 147 appearances, as well as his overall influence in games, were key in the Black Cats' rise from League One to the Premier League between 2022 and 2025.

In need of more depth in the wide areas last summer, Davies was already aware of what Roberts could bring to the table from their Parkhead days, with the former revealing: "I know the manager - I used to work with him when I was younger, so one phone call from him was all I needed."

Roberts has already made a strong impression at St. Andrew's, and was rewarded by seeing his loan move turned permanent in January.

Despite perhaps not always living up to his full hype, the attacker has already provided some magic moments at St. Andrew's in terms of goals and assists - notably a last-gasp equaliser against Leeds United in the thrilling FA Cup clash on February 15th, even if Birmingham were beaten on penalties.

Blues fans, how good a signing has Patrick Roberts been? Comment below!

He has only started a select number of games this term by competing against Carlos Vicente, but there is a school of thought that Davies' side are much more promising in attack with the 29-year-old in the starting XI.

#2179. Europa League preview: AC Milan vs. Ferencvaros – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

AC Milan are back in front of their own fans on Thursday night, hoping to correct their European course against Ferencvaros.

Milan are buoyed by the derby win over Inter at the weekend, and yet in continental competition they have struggled so far having lost two of three. So, the pressure remains on to bounce back and start climbing the Europa League table before it is too late.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In his pre-match press conference, Ruben Amorim admitted that his side needed to find some consistency, especially after the win against Inter. Effectively, his message was that the win would mean little if it wasn’t followed with another three points.

Game date: Thursday, November 4 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Urs Schnyder (VAR: Fähndrich)

As mentioned above, Milan could hardly be going into this game feeling any better after they scored three first-half goals to down their city rivals for a fourth straight time. Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira scored in a 3-1 win that was well engineered by Ruben Amorim.

The Rossoneri continue to demonstrate their potential domestically, even if they remain seven points off top, but in the Europa League things haven’t gone to plan. Losses to Benfica and Bournemouth – both without scoring – either side of the rout of RB Salzburg leave them on three points from three games.

That puts Milan in 24th place in the table on goals scored, which is the final play-off spot. So, a big improvement is needed in the final five games of the league phase in order for the tag of being among the pre-tournament favourites to be justified.

Mario Gila, Rabiot and Moreira all returned to the line-up against Inter, which provided a very noticeable boost. However, there are no new recoveries in view of the match against Ferencvaros, so the depth is still limited.

Fikayo Tomori is in the treatment room after suffering a torn muscle in his right thigh, joining Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze who also remain out. The latter may yet require surgery on a hip issue.

The other major absentee is Mike Maignan, who saw red for shoving Tyler Adams in the face during the last Europa League game against Bournemouth and will be forced to serve a one-match ban, which is less than feared.

The latest from the various media reports suggests that Amorim will field quite a youthful side, as he has done in Europe so far. This means chances should be given to Lorenzo Torriani, Sankhoun Diawara, Ardon Jashari, Davide Bartesaghi, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and potentially more.

Expectations about rotation seem likely to be proven right, with the defence being almost completely changed. Without a back-up, Torriani is indeed given the nod.

Then, the backline is made of a largely rotated group. Filippo Terracciano will start at right-back, whilst Koni De Winter will partner Diawara in the middle of the back four. Bartesaghi returns at left-back.

In midfield, Hutchinson and Cisse will start on the flanks as expected, with Yunus Musah and Jashari given the nod in the middle of the park.

Despite suggestions that Camarda could start, it seems Goncalo Ramos will be given the starting role again.

Predicted Milan XI (4-4-1-1): Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Rabiot; Ramos

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Comotto, Modric, Moreira, Pulisic, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Maignan, Pavlovic, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze, Gabbia, Tomori, Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

This will be the first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros, making it a historic encounter as a result.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match. Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencáros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026/2027.

➤ AC Milan will look to build on their derby success when they welcome an unbeaten Ferencváros side to the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday evening. Ruben Amorim’s team have enjoyed a promising domestic campaign but struggled to replicate that form in Europe, occupying 24th place in the league-phase standings with just three points from their opening three matches. Their Hungarian opponents, meanwhile, sit fourth with a perfect nine-point return and arrive in Italy chasing a fourth consecutive European victory.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter Milan at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing. They suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11. Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures. Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967/68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level. Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

Sankhoun Diawara has been superb so far when called upon, and he’ll replace the ever-present Strahinja Pavlovic here. A big performance would not only reassure the club of his ability (and potential), but it may offer a reason to change January plans.

It feels like a weekly occurrence now, but Goncalo Ramos needs a goal. If Francesco Camarda is not going to start here, the Portuguese needs to prove that there is reason to keep the youngster on the bench. For his sake, as much as the Italian’s.

For the visitors, Kristoffer Zachariassen is the main danger man. Contributing to 11 goals in 21 games so far this season, the 32-year-old will be essential to Ferencvaros getting anything on Thursday.

Then, Mariano Gomez will represent a difficult opponent for whoever leads the Rossoneri’s line. The Argentine defender has been excellent so far this season, and it’s entirely possible that he contributes to a frustrating night.

Despite their rotations, Milan must win here; if they don’t, they’ll wave their Europa League top eight wishes goodbye. There’s enough quality in the starting XI to provide three points, so that will be the expectation.

#2178. Director confirms ‘the next step’ with talks over deal for West Ham man eyed

West Ham loaned out flop striker Niclas Fullkrug in the summer, and his remarkable form since rejoining Werder Bremen has been well documented. The 33-year-old has 12 goals in 11 games this season, earning a recall to Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad and prompting swift talk over a permanent WHUFC exit.

Now, Werder Bremen sporting director Clemens Fritz has spoken publicly about the matter, telling Sky Sports Germany (as relayed by the Hamburger Morgenpost) that the plan is to hold formal talks with the Hammers over a permanent move for Fullkrug.

“The next step is to enter into dialogue with West Ham,” Fritz said. “We will, of course, hold talks about this. Ultimately, we also have to see what the financial package looks like.”

West Ham signed Fullkrug for a hefty fee worth up to £27m in 2024. He had been a prolific scorer in Germany, but there were eyebrows raised over the amount paid given that he was aged 31 at the time.

Those concerns were justified, as Fullkrug failed to make a positive impact in English football. Across all competitions, he managed three goals and two assists in 29 games for the Hammers, so his summer exit to Werder Bremen was a much-needed one.

The German has been a prolific scorer in his home country across his career, but few expected him to find the form of his life on the return to Werder Bremen. Fullkrug has 12 goals in 11 games for the club, with Saturday’s 1-0 loss to VfB Stuttgart marking the first Bundesliga game he has failed to score in since August 30th.

His call-up to Klopp’s Germany squad shows just how well he has been doing. Few WHUFC fans would have expected such success given the standard of his performances over two years in East London.

When players out on loan hit impressive form, it is often met with clamour for their return. However, that is highly unlikely to be the case for Fullkrug.

His circumstances are different. Not only did West Ham pay out a big transfer fee and sizeable wages, but he turns 34 later this season, so will likely have eyes on seeing out the twilight years of his career enjoying his football back in his home country.

Fullkrug’s stint at WHUFC is one best forgotten, and neither he nor the club should have a problem with bringing their affiliation to a permanent end. He can focus on maintaining his form and happily seeing out his career in Germany while the Hammers get his wages off the books for good.

#2177. West Ham dodge £10.5m transfer bullet and Stoke City will laugh

West Ham United have had a turbulent start back in the Championship, with the Hammers set to enter a new era under Scott Parker after dismissing Nuno Espírito Santo, and the incoming head coach may already be feeling some transfer relief.

After six wins in their first 13 league games, and following back-to-back home defeats to Southampton and West Bromwich Albion, Nuno Espírito Santo was relieved of his duties at West Ham and has since been replaced by former Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker oversaw a 3-3 draw away to Cardiff City in midweek in his first game in charge, and will already be well aware of the improvements that need to be made to the squad, with one eye likely already on the January transfer window.

It was a tricky summer window for the Hammers, who took a while to get up and running, though they may be feeling some relief right now after missing out on an eight-figure player who has so far failed to set the world alight at his new club.

Following relegation from the Premier League to the Championship, West Ham sought to overhaul their recruitment strategy, bringing in former PSV Eindhoven, Rangers, and Copenhagen Head of Scouting Nils Koppen to spearhead their squad building.

It took a while to get underway, but the likes of Arne Engels, Manor Solomon, Joel Piroe, Edvin Austbo, Joel Veltman, and Divine Mukasa headed to the London Stadium, and among the numerous other names linked with a switch to the Hammers was then-Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

Sorba Thomas - Championship Stats 2025/26

Thomas, 27, was coming off the back of an excellent personal campaign with the Potters, with whom he registered ten goals and 15 assists in 52 appearances across all competitions, as Alan Nixon confirmed via his Patreon that the Welsh international was a player of interest to the Hammers.

The winger spent time in the West Ham academy as a youngster, but was released at an early age, and a homecoming appeared on the cards before Premier League interest turned his head the other way.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

Stoke, having lost each of their three opening league games of the season, were understandably reluctant to lose Thomas, who was undoubtedly their most important player from the prior campaign, directly contributing to over 40 per cent of the Potters' goals in the Championship that year.

However, following promotion to the Premier League, Hull City were keen to add some strength and depth in the final third, and after a drawn-out transfer saga, agreed a fee in the region of around £10.5 million that saw the Welshman head to Humberside.

By this point, it became clear that West Ham, despite breaking the EFL record fee for Engels, were reluctant to match that fee, having signed both Solomon and Austbo as well, and whilst neither of those have necessarily shone as yet, they may well have dodged a bullet in Thomas.

Since his arrival at the MKM Stadium, Thomas has made five Premier League appearances, three of those being starts, grabbing one assist against Everton.

However, in the very same game, he gave the ball away cheaply to allow Thierno Barry to score for the visitors, whilst on his full debut against Newcastle United, he gave away an unprecedented penalty.

In that past couple of games, Thomas has found himself as an unused substitute against Brentford, and out of the matchday squad entirely against Ipswich Town, with Tigers head coach Sergej Jakirovic openly criticising his displays in training.

It's not exactly been an ideal start for Thomas, who certainly has time on his side to turn things around with Hull, but has failed to make the desired impression thus far, as West Ham must be relieved whilst Stoke will be laughing.

Have West Ham dodged a bullet in missing out on Thomas? Was selling him the best thing that Stoke could have done? Will the Welshman prove to be a hit for Hull? Share your thoughts below!

Although things aren't totally rosy at West Ham right now, a poor attitude in the squad would only have made things worse, and given Parker more of a headache to deal with.

Had he joined the Hammers, there is no guarantee poor performances in training would have ensued, though whilst West Ham may be relieved after this news, Stoke must be laughing.

Since Thomas left, no other team has picked up more points than the Potters in the Championship, winning eight and losing just one of their last 11 league games, with the Welshman's exit coinciding with a switch in system and subsequent climb up the table.

Stoke lost their best player from last season and have gotten better, whilst making a significant profit in the process, as Mark Robins must be laughing at how things have played out.

#2176. The Celtic 'rollercoaster' Mika Baur is getting used to & how he spends his days off

It is easy to forget that Mika Baur only turned 22 over the summer. The German midfielder displayed maturity beyond his years in Celtic's captivating Europa League victory over Besiktas on Thursday evening, chasing lost causes, contributing defensively, and progressing play forward when the opportunity arrived.

It was his finest performance since joining the club for an initial fee of £4.5 million from Paderborn in August.

Baur compared his first few months in Glasgow to riding a rollercoaster, with downtime away from the football pitch proving rare.

"There’s no time to think about it! We are playing every three days and I really try to fight and bring my heart on the field all the time," Baur said. "Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t, but I hope people understand as a young player it can be tough to be comfortable in a new country, a new culture and new club.

"But I really try my best. I have felt good in my first few months but it is a bit of a rollercoaster.

"Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans, getting the call-up to the national team was a big honour. You feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost but I am getting used to it."

This is Baur's first time living away from home. He credits his partner for making the transition to Scotland smoother, even if chances to play some golf are limited.

"I’m grateful to my girlfriend as she does most things and makes it comfortable at home," Baur continued. "The club also have people who have helped us a lot to settle.

"But you don’t get much time – you get home and lie on the couch!

"It’s not all stressful though. It’s also nice to go somewhere new and learn the city, get to coffee shops and restaurants.

"We’ve been to the beach, we’ve been to Edinburgh, we try to see a lot on our day off.

"I also play golf – so I’ve come to the home of golf! I’ve only managed to get to the driving range though. When you are playing every three days it’s a bit much to play nine or 18 holes.

"My father and brother play so hopefully the weather will be okay around Christmas to maybe manage a few holes."

Thursday's win over Besiktas wasn't quite a hole-in-one, but it marked a pivotal forward step in Celtic's Europa League campaign.

Finally up and running after consecutive defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, Baur gave credit to a raucous home support.

"The fans helped a lot," he explained. "You could feel the energy. It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win – it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well.

"It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.

"There is always pressure to win here, to win every three days. That’s what we all want. In the last two games it wasn’t possible for us. We knew it wasn’t good enough but here we played well and deserved it."

"The win was important after some tough weeks," Baur continued. "But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good.

"There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves. We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift.

"It was important to get those three points and we deserved it. Hopefully we can go forward with confidence from this game."

Despite his stellar showing on Thursday, Baur missed out on Jurgen Klopp's latest Germany squad. He made his senior international debut against Serbia last month as the former Liverpool manager had named two separate squads for four fixtures.

Klopp's group was reduced this time around, though Baur will return to the under-21s.

"I can understand," Baur said of the snub. "There are so many unbelievable players in the squad, especially in my position.

"We’re talking about guys from Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. I just do my best and hopefully they can see I am developing and improving.

"I’m still with the under-21s for the games against Belgium and Croatia, so that will be good. European matches like Thursday can only help and I have to hope they see.

"I’m still young but I’ll keep doing my best and we’ll see what happens next time."

#2174. All 2026/27 EFL Championship clubs ranked by how much they spend on wages every week

The 2026/27 Championship season has already sprung surprises at both ends of the table, with clubs who weren't necessarily expected to mount promotion challenges already setting the pace, whilst others find themselves in dire straits in the bottom-half.

That in itself is one of the beauties of the second tier, that any side is capable of beating another on their day, regardless of the amount of investment which has been ploughed into squads or the strength-in-depth at any manager's disposal.

Football finance has become a dominant topic in recent times, with some clubs finding themselves in extremely concerning circumstances due to spending beyond their means in a bid to achieve short and long-term ambitions.

With that being said, Football League World have looked at how much each of the Championship's 24 clubs are ESTIMATED to be spending on wages per week, according to Capology.

It may come as no surprise that newly-promoted Lincoln City are believed to have the division's lowest wage bill.

Despite breaking their transfer record for the signing of Danish forward, Mikkel Ladefoged, the Imps are believed to be paying out just £161,750 per week.

Portsmouth boss, John Mousinho, was backed in the summer transfer window to add further quality to his squad, and although the South Coast club have shown signs of progression, they are said to have the second-lowest wage bill in the Championship.

According to the aforementioned site, chairman Michael Eisner is only spending £222,000 per week on wages at Fratton Park.

Bolton Wanderers are said to have the division's third-lowest wage bill following their return to the Championship after a seven-year exile.

It has been debated whether Steven Schumacher was backed enough in the transfer window amid the Whites' mixed start to the campaign, although the fact the ownership are said to be spending just £231,000 per week on wages, some will say that survival is a strong achievement.

Next up are Charlton Athletic, who returned to the Championship last summer after five years in League One.

Having survived at the first time of asking, Nathan Jones will be hoping his side can progress up the Championship table in time, even if a weekly wage bill of £255,800 is believed to be the fourth-lowest in the second tier.

Queens Park Rangers have enjoyed a largely positive start to the season, but will be hoping the remainder of the campaign doesn't follow a similar pattern to 2025/26.

The Hoops have certainly cut their costs in recent years, though, having failed to trouble the promotion picture since being relegated 11 years ago, with it now being estimated that the club are only paying £290,200 a week in wages.

Millwall have invested rather heavily in the squad at Alex Neil's disposal in recent times, meaning it may surprise people that they are estimated to have the sixth-lowest wage bill in the Championship.

The Lions surprised many by finishing third last season, and if they did achieve an unexpected promotion, there is no doubt the payroll in SE16 would have been significantly higher than £296,000 per week.

AI has had its say on which clubs are currently the biggest sleeping giants outside the Premier League

Blackburn Rovers are up next, with the East Lancashire club's financial situation under the Venky's being well-publicised in recent years.

The one-time Premier League champions have, in recent seasons, fluctuated between play-off and relegation battles, and this season will be hoping to upset the odds whilst having a wage bill of £297,500 per week.

Preston North End's start to the season has been nothing short of dire, even after a summer in which the Lilywhites broke their transfer record for the permanent signing of Alfie Devine from Tottenham Hotspur.

Although still early days into his reign, Graham Alexander is yet to turn the tide following the sacking of Paul Heckingbottom, and relegation to League One would certainly result in cuts to an estimated weekly payroll of £302,000.

Bristol City endured a summer of change, with Michael Skubala taking over at Ashton Gate whilst recruiting some exciting names such as Sam Tickle, Lorent Tolaj and Dom Ballard.

The Robins will be hoping to put a disappointing 2025/26 campaign behind them and challenge for the play-offs once more, even if such ambition isn't entirely reflected by a weekly wage bill of £306,500.

Despite seeing high-profile investors such as Snoop Dogg and Luka Modrić involved with the club, Swansea City still sit in the bottom-half when it comes to estimated wage bills in the Championship.

However, a figure of just £323,000 per week in that regard hasn't stopped Vitor Matos' side from enjoying an extremely impressive start to the season, and one they will hope continues right up to matchday 46.

#2173. Three goals from 1.09 xG: £20m star’s stunning form inspires Birmingham City’s rise to the top of the Championship

Birmingham City defeated fellow promotion hopefuls Swansea City on Saturday, making it six wins from the last seven to move to 1st in the Championship. BCFC have put in some fantastic team performances in this run, but as far as individual efforts go, it is hard to overlook that of Jay Stansfield.

The £20m Blues man has moved back to striker in August Priske‘s absence for the last two games, and he has netted three goals. In victories over Millwall and the Swans, Stansfield has over-performed his xG of 1.09 by 1.91 (FotMob), providing a timely reminder of his goalscoring threat at St. Andrew’s.

Playing as an attacking midfielder, Stansfield has been more of a facilitator than a goalscorer in recent times, with his well-rounded game and fantastic work rate seeing him retain a key role in Chris Davies’ side. Blues fans needed no reminder of his importance, but the 24-year-old’s return to the scoresheet in the last two games has affirmed just how good he is as the lead man up top.

Stansfield is one of the faces of Birmingham City’s rebuild. He impressed on loan despite relegation in the 2023/24 season, and was the statement signing of Tom Wagner and co ahead of their record-breaking League One title win, joining permanently for a reported fee of up to £20m.

23 goals in 44 games across the 2024/25 campaign helped inspire City back to the Championship, and he followed that up with 11 goals in all competitions last term. However, a move out of his natural striker role has seen goals decrease for Stansfield.

Before November started, Stansfield had just three league goals in 2026. As said before, his work rate in and out of possession and his technical ability in knitting attacks together meant he has held an influential role regardless – for the most part. However, three goals in four days have made the Tiverton-born forward pivotal in BCFC’s rise to the Championship summit.

Stansfield was everywhere against Swansea City. Not only did he score twice, but he created two chances and one big chance, took seven shots and covered plenty of ground (FotMob). His heatmap showed that, despite playing as the traditional striker, he was still dropping deep and drifting wide to pick up the ball and keep the Swans’ defence thinking.

It was the sort of performance that everyone knows Stansfield is capable of. He led by example in terms of both attribution and ability as Davies’ side moved top.

Birmingham City’s faith in Davies has paid off. After doubts over whether he could lead them to the next level, he has weathered the storm and turned his side into deserving Championship leaders.

The Welshman has a tough call to make amid Stansfield’s return to goalscoring form though. At striker, it feels like his entire skillset is being used as he finds more shooting opportunities.

Stansfield is more of a scoring threat at striker compared to attacking midfield. However, the form of Danish ace Priske at the top of the pitch cannot be ignored, and he is not capable of dropping into a deeper role like his attacking counterpart.

It is highly likely that Stansfield drops back into the no. 10 role when Priske is fit again. But, recent performances and historic stats suggest that Blues get their best out of their big-money star when he’s deployed at the top of the pitch.

It is a welcome dilemma for Davies to have, as Birmingham City enter the break on a high.

#2171. Jim Goodwin says Dundee Utd are eager to keep momentum going against Motherwell

Jim Goodwin insists Dundee United are raring to go against Motherwell following their unwanted free weekend.

After a morale-boosting 2-2 draw with Celtic at Parkhead which extended their unbeaten run to six games, the Tannadice side had to miss their next William Hill Premiership fixture against Hearts as the Jambos had a Premier Sports Cup semi-final match against Hibernian.

Ahead of the visit of the Steelmen to Tannadice on Saturday, Goodwin told DUTV: “We’ve had a really good week training, obviously with no football at the weekend. That can be a little bit frustrating because, especially off the back of such a good performance against Celtic, you’re desperate for the next game to come around quick.

“But we’ve had a solid week’s training. The boys have done seven or eight sessions over the four days that we’ve been in. We’re having to drag them off the training pitch at times because they’re so keen to stay out there.

“Hopefully, there should be a lot of fresh legs there and hopefully we can go and give a good account of ourselves and maintain this unbeaten run that we’re on.”

Celtic's 'Che Guevaras' should show their fellow fans some respect at this year's AGM Marink Reedijk lays down Aberdeen challenge to Hibs team after Hearts win

United’s last defeat, coincidentally, was a 3-0 loss to Motherwell at Fir Park in September where Goodwin’s side were reduced to 10 men in 14 minutes when Emmanuel Agyei was sent off for a foul on Alex Lowry.

Goodwin is reading little into that defeat. He said: “For the first 15 minutes I didn’t think there was a great deal between the two teams. But then we get the red card to Emmanuel Agyei and that changes the whole game.

“They’ve got good pace. With the man extra they can really find pockets of space all over the pitch and they punished us on the night. But it’s a very hard game for me to analyse because of the fact that we were down to 10 men for 75 minutes.

“So I think tomorrow, if we can keep 11 men on the pitch, that would certainly be a start. I think 11 v 11, it makes for a very entertaining game of football. Two really good teams, two technical teams.

“They’ve got that attacking threat and that bit of firepower at the top with the pace they have. But we also believe we’ve got real firepower ourselves and real quality in the middle of the pitch where hopefully we can get that bit of control that we want.”

#2170. Sheffield Utd should target Ipswich Town & Plymouth Argyle transfers this January

After a slow start to the season, Sheffield United have started to find form under Chris Wilder as they push for a play-off place.

The off-field situation at Bramall Lane contributed to a frustrating summer transfer window, with many Blades fans feeling that Wilder was left short in the market.

As we know, the Yorkshire outfit aren’t in a position to splash huge sums, and that’s not going to change in the New Year.

Nevertheless, Wilder will hope that there is room to do some business, and he has shown numerous times over the years that he has an eye for a player.

Despite Sheffield United’s impressive recent form, it’s clear that fresh additions are needed, and the boss will no doubt feel a few positions should be addressed.

Therefore, reports linking the Blades to ex-Birmingham left-back Emmanuel Longelo, who is starring for Motherwell, make sense, as he would certainly improve the group.

Football League World has named and ranked the SEVEN most emotionally exhausting EFL Championship clubs to support right now...

But, he may not be the only new face through the door, and here we look at TWO other players that should be on Sheffield United’s radar…

It seems inevitable that Wilder will be targeting attacking players, as the Blades have sometimes lacked a spark in the final third.

One player who could make a big difference is Ipswich Town’s Anis Mehmeti, who has proven himself in the Championship over the years with the Tractor Boys and Bristol City.

The attacking midfielder is way down the pecking order at Portman Road right now, and whilst he rejected summer moves in a bid to fight for his place, he will recognise that he must leave for regular game time, as he hasn’t even made Gary O’Neil’s squad for a Premier League game.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

So, he’s certain to be available, and, from a football perspective, Mehmeti is exactly what the Blades are lacking. He looks to find pockets of space, he can play on the half turn, and, most importantly, he is capable of beating his man and creating chances.

The obvious concern is that a host of Championship clubs will also be tracking Mehmeti, but Sheffield United will be able to offer first-team football and a key role in the side, and a loan move means this could be very realistic.

Wilder does have several strikers to choose from, but they are lacking a number nine with genuine pace who can run in behind and offer that threat.

There will be a belief at the club that Ryan One could become that player, but he has suffered bad luck on the injury front, and he is still unproven at this level.

Either way, they could still do with a young, hungry striker who has good physical attributes, and Plymouth’s Bim Pepple ticks all the boxes on that front.

It certainly won’t be easy to prise him from Home Park in January, especially as Argyle chase promotion, but we know that money talks, and the appeal of moving to Sheffield United for the player is obvious.

Which one player would you like Sheffield United to sign in January? Let us know in the comments below.

Given his age and room for potential, Wilder would surely try to convince the hierarchy that it is a long-term investment that could pay-off in style, and a reported 'seven-figure' release clause means this may be a possibility.

Then, as outlined above, he has qualities that Sheffield United need, and you would back Pepple to handle the step up to the second tier, as whilst he is raw, he has plenty of talent and could flourish around better players.

#2169. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2168. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Harry Maguire-5.5            Was decent in the first half but wasn’t much of an answer to Tottenham going forward in the second half

Lisandro Martinez-5      Took his eyes off the ball, resulting in conceding a late goal off Solanke.

Luke Shaw-6      Went up high on the pitch and remained a threat with his overlapping threat. Was involved in the scuffle that got Bentancur a red card for headbutting.

Kobbie Mainoo-6.5        Brilliant defensive tackle to deny Tottenham in the 68th minute. Remained composed in tight spaces against a physical Tottenham midfield.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

Carlos Baleba (58’)-6.5  A decent debut overall for the Cameroon international. He put in a couple of dangerous balls up the field, including a clear ball to Mbeumo on a counter, who was denied by Kinsky.

Diogo Dalot (58’)-6      Provided a decent attacking threat when brought on around the hour mark.

Joshua Zirkzee (58’)-6   Showed plenty of promise and was a threat after he was brought in around the hour mark.

#2167. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2166. Sunderland plot move for ex-Southampton and West Ham star to replace Le Bris

Premier League side Sunderland could target ex-Southampton and West Ham United player Jose Fonte to replace Regis Le Bris.

Now in November, sackings are happening more and more across English football. Regis Le Bris has credit in the bank for his promotion from the Championship with Sunderland in 2024/25, while also guiding them into the Europa League in 2025/26, but pressure is mounting.

His side are bottom of the Premier League heading into today's game against Chelsea at the Stadium of Light, with Sunderland having also lost to Dinamo Zagreb at home on Thursday. Now, it could mean Jose Fonte comes in to replace him.

Fonte spent the most significant period of his English career with Southampton, joining from Crystal Palace in January 2010 and making 288 appearances across seven years at St. Mary's.

He was instrumental in the Saints' remarkable rise from League One to the Premier League, becoming a hugely respected figure before earning a move to West Ham in January 2017. His spell in east London was much shorter, however, lasting just over a year and producing 24 appearances.

Fonte went on to enjoy successful spells with Lille and Braga before finishing his playing career at Casa Pia in 2026, bringing the curtain down on an extraordinary 24-year senior career. Since then, he has been coaching under Le Bris at Sunderland, joining back in July.

Now, Alan Nixon has revealed Sunderland are plotting for him to replace Le Bris in the dugout. He says that the 42-year-old is highly regarded by the club's chiefs and that they are eyeing him if Le Bris moves on.

Fonte was far more than just a dependable centre-back during his playing days because he was a genuine leader, particularly at Southampton, where he became one of the most influential figures in the club's modern history and rise through League One and the Championship and to the Premier League.

He captained the Saints through their rise from League One to the top flight, helped establish them and later enjoyed success with Portugal and Lille. Given his presence, communication skills and ability to command respect in a dressing room, it is hardly surprising that he wanted to move into coaching.

FLW have ranked all 24 Championship clubs on how far they have fallen from their historical glory days, including Blackburn and West Ham.

What did you make of Jose Fonte at your club? Comment below!

Sunderland might be a step too far for him as a head coach at this early stage, but his personality and leadership qualities suggest he could eventually become much more than an assistant. He has the attributes to develop into a manager in his own right but Sunderland not going for a more established and experienced alternative will be a head scratcher for many.

Back in July, speaking to The Sunderland Echo, it was revealed why Fonte was brought in by the club’s director of football Florent Ghisolfi. He said his experience of football at the highest level would be a big benefit to the club this season, as they are competing in Europe for the first time in over 50 years.

Ghisolfi explained Fonte's "strong leadership skills" which would help complement the current coaching group. Speaking about the former Southampton and West Ham figuure, he said: “Jose joins our coaching team with a wealth of experience as a player at the top level.

“He will bring that experience, along with tremendous energy, to a technical staff that is already performing outstandingly under the guidance of Regis.

We believe those qualities, combined with his strong leadership skills, will add great value to our club as we look to push forward both in the Premier League and on the European stage. We’re delighted to welcome Jose to Sunderland AFC.”

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2165. Why James Morrison and West Brom fans are tipping 26-year-old star for a Premier League rise as impeccable form continues

West Brom sit 5th in the table after a 3-0 win over Millwall on Saturday made it six games without defeat. Isaac Price and Jayson Molumby made the headlines as they both scored one and set up another, but it was a fantastic team performance from WBA who strengthen their promotion credentials with every passing match.

Although not a regular on the scoresheet, one man never far away from praise is Ousmane Diakite. And, once again, the Malian midfielder was excellent on Saturday, playing the full 90 minutes in midfield as the Baggies stormed to victory.

Focusing on the win over Millwall, Diakite was key in his usual role of winning duels, guarding the backline and keeping the ball moving. Primarily operating on the left of the midfield two, the West Brom man completed 51 of his 58 passes, five of which were into the final third while one created a chance.

In duels is where the 26-year-old found most of his success though, as has been the case all season. Diakite won seven duels in total: six on the ground and one in the air. He also completed three tackles, made two interceptions and four recoveries (FotMob).

This latest effort contributed to his eye-catching totals across the Championship campaign to date. No central midfielder has won more than his 92 duels, and he ranks amongst the league’s best in his position for aerial duels won (28 – top 2%), clearances (44 – top 2%) and defensive contributions (98 – top 3%).

On the ball, WBA star Diakite has completed 595 passes (top 9%), made 86 line-breaking passes (top 23%), made 13 successful dribbles (top 8%) and won 23 fouls (top 4%). As far as his stats go, he has been one of the Championship’s most effective midfielders of the season so far in all key areas apart from chance creation and goalscoring with those responsibilities falling to Albion stars Price, Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Aune Heggebo and more.

After a challenging start in a West Brom shirt, Diakite proved his worth in last season’s relegation fight under James Morrison and deservedly earned a new deal. He has got better and better in the 2026/27 campaign, and is a crucial part of an Albion side that looks ready for a promotion challenge.

In the build up to the Millwall game, Baggies boss Morrison was asked whether Diakite was a Premier League player in the making. Speaking to reporter Steve Tudgay, he said: “Yes he is. With us!”

Similarly, former West Brom man Paul Robinson recently told the Express and Star: “He has Premier League attributes, when you look at him”.

Not only do Diakite’s stats back this up, but so do the rave reviews of WBA supporters. Over the past week or so, numerous fans have shared their belief in his potential on X:

Ousmane Diakite WILL be a premier league footballer. Hopefully with us but time will tell #wba

Diakite walks into a bottom half Prem team all day for me #wba

Diakite could get into the Man united midfield all day, his improvement since joining has been unreal to watch #wba

West Brom fans will be hoping Diakite’s form continues. If it does, he may well get his deserved step up to the top flight at The Hawthorns.

#2163. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2162. Ex-Rangers star signs for new club in second tier after weeks as free agent

Former Rangers midfielder Greg Docherty has signed for Preston North End as a free agent.

The 30-year-old has been without a club since leaving Charlton Athletic by mutual agreement near the end of the summer transfer window, despite having captained them to promotion from League One a year before.

With the Addicks continually strengthening for the Championship, he found himself out of favour and it was agreed he could move on in search of first team football.

Former Motherwell boss Graham Alexander recently took over at Preston and was tipped in recent weeks to make a move for Docherty, after admitting he was looking at free agents. That has now come to fruition.

Preston announced the signing today and Docherty told their website: “I’m really proud to be here, to have this badge on my chest and to be part of a club that’s steeped in history. When I told my family, they were all excited and willing me to get it done.

“I’m just thankful that we managed to do it. Coming down from Scotland and playing in England, Preston’s a very good team to get to for my family and I’ve always kept an eye on them.

Derek McInnes news, interviews and updates on the Rangers manager The quietly effective Rangers star McInnes says inspires dressing-room confidence

“I’ve always loved playing at Deepdale but haven’t won very often there, so hopefully that will change now. When I was an opposition player, I always found it really difficult. I’ve got family in the north of England and this move just really ticks all the boxes.

“To be a Preston player is something I’ve always wanted to do and I’m really proud to have finally done it.”

Docherty has been training with Alexander's side already and added: “From the moment I walked in here, I got a really good feeling from speaking to the manager and all the coaching staff.

“When I see how passionate the manager is about turning our current situation around, it excites me and I want to also help change things. I see real quality in the dressing room and I know we can improve if we keep working hard.

“The manager’s training demands are very high, and I’ve come in and really enjoyed it. I’ve enjoyed the soreness after it, I’ve enjoyed the tiredness after it, but I feel much better for it and all the lads do too.

“The boys are saying they’re getting fitter, which is massive in this league, and I just can’t wait to get going alongside them out on the pitch.”

Alexander said: “We’re really pleased to bring Greg in. He’s been a captain, won promotions and knows the game inside out.

“Greg’s vocal, fit and motivated, which are all the key things you look for in a professional footballer.

“He has settled into the group really quickly and has a real willingness to show what he can do.”

#2161. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”
